items.body: Test Dept and the Welsh performance company Brith Gof release “Gododdin: 2026 Remaster” on 4 December 2026 via Artoffact Records. The set expands their 1989 album into a 3CD/1DVD box, alongside a separate red vinyl LP and a digital edition. “Gododdin” is based on Y Gododdin, the earliest surviving Welsh-language poem, written around 600 AD. It tells of 300 Celtic warriors who attacked 100,000 invading Angles and lost. Test Dept and Brith Gof first staged the piece as a live performance at an abandoned Rover car factory in Cardiff in December 1988, using 600 tons of sand, 50 trees and 30 wrecked cars on a set that flooded as the show went on. Further performances followed in 1989 in Italy, the Netherlands, West Germany and Scotland. The original 1989 studio album was produced by Ken Thomas at Jacobs Studios from Test Dept’s existing studio and field recordings, augmented with brass and wind courtesy of Brith Gof’s John E R Hardy and bagpipes from Alistair Adams. Paul Jamrozy’s voice runs alongside the Welsh-language vocals of Lis Hughes Jones. “Gododdin: 2026 Remaster” widens that original 7-track album with 19 tracks that have not previously been released. The first disc is a reworked version built from newly unearthed multitrack tapes of the early studio sessions, put together by Test Dept founder members Graham Cunnington and Paul Jamrozy during the summer of 2026. The second disc carries a live recording from one of the 1989 performances, staged in a quarry in Polverigi, Italy. The DVD holds a documentary from the period, with live footage and interviews with performers, academics and other experts. Compiled by Test Dept with input from Brith Gof members Lis Hughes Jones, John E R Hardy and Heike Roms, the set was remastered by Paul Lavigne at Kontrast Mastering. It comes in a 5-panel ecopak with a 24-page booklet of archival imagery and writing, including an essay by author and Test Dept researcher Alexei Monroe. The artwork for both the box and the separate red vinyl LP was redesigned by Paul Jamrozy and Stefan Alt (ant-zen); the vinyl edition carries the original album plus one previously unreleased track and a printed insert. Ahead of the box set, Test Dept released the advance single “Gwr a Aeth Gatraeth / Prologue (Early Studio Sessions, Reworked 2026)” on 2 October 2026, available on Spotify, Apple Music and YouTube. “Gododdin: 2026 Remaster” is the second in Test Dept’s ongoing series of archival reissues on Artoffact Records, who signed the band in 2025 for catalogue reissues and a new album. It follows the 4xCD “Industrial Overture: Studio & Live Recordings 1982-1985”, released a year earlier. Artoffact will also release new Test Dept material in 2027. A separate event ties into the reissue: Test Dept and Brith Gof take part in a discussion and Q&A about “Gododdin” at Chapter in Cardiff on 24 October, as part of the Experimentica festival’s 25th-anniversary programme. About Test Dept Test Dept formed in London in the early 1980s as an industrial music group built around live percussion on scrap metal and found objects. In 1988 and 1989, the band collaborated with the Welsh avant-garde theatre company Brith Gof on “Gododdin”, staging it first at an abandoned car factory in Cardiff and then on tour in Italy, the Netherlands, West Germany and Scotland. The 1989 studio album version was produced by Ken Thomas at Jacobs Studios. Test Dept returned to active release and performance in the 2020s. In 2025, the band signed to Artoffact Records for a series of catalogue reissues alongside a new studio album. The first of those reissues, the 4xCD “Industrial Overture: Studio & Live Recordings 1982-1985”, arrived in October 2025. “Gododdin: 2026 Remaster”, out 4 December 2026, is the second. Current members Graham Cunnington and Paul Jamrozy built new versions of the early “Gododdin” studio sessions for the reissue during the summer of 2026, working from recently unearthed multitrack tapes. Test Dept continue to tour, with confirmed UK and European dates running from October 2026 into the summer of 2027, and have a new studio album due via Artoffact in 2027. About Brith Gof Brith Gof is a Welsh performance company known for large-scale, site-specific theatre work that drew on Welsh history and language. Co-founded by figures including Mike Pearson, Lis Hughes Jones and Clifford McLucas, the company staged “Gododdin” with Test Dept in Cardiff in 1988, adapting the early Welsh poem Y Gododdin into a promenade performance inside a disused car factory. Hughes Jones, John E R Hardy and Heike Roms were directly involved in compiling “Gododdin: 2026 Remaster” alongside Test Dept.
items._cn_summary: Test Dept与威尔士表演团体Brith Gof合作的《Gododdin》基于公元600年左右现存最早的威尔士语史诗，讲述300名凯尔特勇士以寡敌众的故事。原始现场表演于1988年在卡迪夫废弃的Rover汽车工厂举行，舞台使用600吨沙子、50棵树和30辆废弃汽车，并随着演出进行而逐渐被水淹没。1989年录音室专辑由Ken Thomas制作，融合了田野录音、铜管与风乐元素，配以威尔士语人声。2026年新版扩展为3CD加1DVD套装，新增19首未发表作品，包括从新发现的多轨磁带重新构建的早期录音室版本、1989年意大利采石场现场录音，以及包含采访与影像的纪录片。整体呈现工业声响、田野录音与凯尔特文化叙事的跨界融合。

items.body: Curbside Lambsear Put Rings On All My Fingers To Weigh Down My Hands Members of The Umlauts and caroline find scrappy joy in dissonant chaos mixed with cinematic grandeur Put Rings On All My Fingers To Weigh Down My Hands by Curbside Lambsear This is an intriguingly hard-to-pin-down debut from London’s Curbside Lambsear, AKA Magdalena McLean and Annabelle Mödlinger. Having met while playing in the (still active) art punk band The Umlauts, the duo assembled this lengthy EP in a patchwork fashion. You wouldn't know it. There’s a coherent sense of purpose to these five tracks, as well as a free-roaming attitude when it comes to genre. The post punk-tinged opener, ‘No Ordinary Word’, slouches in on heavy-limbed drums and thick, dubby bass, Mödlinger's insouciant vocals... items._cn_summary: Curbside Lambsear 由 Magdalena McLean 与 Annabelle Mödlinger 组成，二人相识于艺术朋克乐队 The Umlauts，随后以拼贴方式录制了这张包含五首曲目的长 EP。作品呈现出连贯的艺术目的与自由的跨类型姿态：不协和的混乱与电影般的壮丽感并存。开场曲以厚重的鼓点与浓郁的 dub 式贝斯铺陈，演唱者漫不经心的声线在不安定的节奏上滑行，整体氛围松弛却带有实验锋芒。乐评指出这是一张难以简单归类的首作，融合了后朋克的骨架与前卫即兴的肌理，对偏爱实验与暗潮交织的听众而言具有较强吸引力。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — There is nothing better than a short, mysterious introduction featuring a siren-like voice to keep the Canterbury spirit alive; that is how "Swedish Love" begins. Much like on Before the Light, the track features sinuous melodies, reminiscent of a roller coaster ride that never stops, even when it momentarily slows down. The English duo consists of Ryan Stevenson, playing piano, synthesizers, Hammond organ, Mellotron, and guitar, and Andrea Moneta on drums and percussion. They are joined by guest flautist Theo Travis (known for his work with Gong and David Sylvian) and Caroline Joy Clarke, who lends her ethereal vocals to the backing harmonies."Eternal Return" showcases National Health's more eccentric compositional side; eschewing classic jazz-rock, it aligns instead with the genre's most esoteric and absurd aspects, both aesthetically and musically. It is also worth highlighting the clever use of contrast between the more energetic, aggressive sections and the more atmospheric ones, such as in "Sanger." "Sellanr�," by contrast, is more minimalist; the piano enters the mix, revealing another facet of the duo that moves beyond mere nostalgia. It is reminiscent of Brian Eno's solo albums from the 1970s.It is on the track "V" that abrasive textures collide with the flute, recalling the alchemy found in the song "Binoculars" from National Health's album Of Queues and Cures. The layering of synthesizers and symphonic arrangements, alongside the Mellotron and a dark-sounding organ, lends the track an orchestral, at times dissonant, sheen, creating one of the album's highlights; comparisons to King Crimson do not seem out of place, either."Being and Time" has a highly dramatic, theatrical atmosphere, driven by the guitar and then a cloud of keyboards that at times reminded me of Present, though without reaching those abyssal extremes. Towards the end, Caroline Joy Clarke's vocals and a Fripp-esque guitar cascade cause that mist to descend to the ground, enveloping everything before the cycle begins anew at "Zero," where a spacey vibe once again takes over the keyboards.In "The Noble Shirker," the bass lines stand out before the guitar enters and the Mellotron joins in, creating a cascading melodic line reminiscent of Mike Oldfield. There is a touch of Eddie Jobson's atmospheric keyboard style, and it is at this point that guest saxophonist Mike Benson joins the mix, adding a new layer of color and warmth. As the sonic haze clears, we witness the transformations at play, a feat of magic and realized esotericism; just as the teapot from the Gong trilogy morphed into a dangerous, lurking scorpion, that saxophone, evoking Mel Collins's work with King Crimson, pushed Zopp's musical intensity to near-maximum velocity.
items._genre: Canterbury Scene / jazz-rock / progressive rock / experimental
items._cn_summary: Zopp是一支英国二人组合，延续坎特伯雷派（Canterbury Scene）的传统路线，融合爵士摇滚、前卫摇滚与实验元素。核心成员Ryan Stevenson负责钢琴、合成器、Hammond风琴、Mellotron与吉他，Andrea Moneta担任鼓与打击乐，客座乐手Theo Travis的长笛与Mike Benson的萨克斯为作品增添层次。专辑在坎特伯雷的怪诞爵士摇滚底色上，融入Brian Eno式的极简氛围段落、King Crimson式的尖锐不协和和声以及Mike Oldfield式旋律流动。人声被作为氛围层使用，与合成器群、Mellotron共同构建戏剧化、带有仪式感的声场。整体编排注重能量段落与氛围段落之间的对比，旋律线在循环与变奏中不断推进，形成兼具神秘感与张力的听觉体验。

items.body: CATASTROFE CLUB have reached the point where the extinction of humanity begins to sound suspiciously like good news. On Un Dia Mejor, Josep M. Herrera and David Molina survey civilization’s wreckage with the composure of two men who have already accepted that we’ve been hurtling toward disaster since about WW1. The Granollers duo’s fourth single previews UN FUTURO TRANQUILO, their fourth album, due this October through Periphylla Records. Following the trilogy that defined their earlier work, the record opens another chapter for a project whose interests have always stretched far beyond any useful genre designation. Post-punk, darkwave, electronics, post-rock and pop all pass through the machinery, with Herrera’s rough spoken delivery sitting somewhere between public announcement, philosophical complaint and the guy at the end of the bar who has finally assembled enough evidence to prove civilization was a clerical error. Un Dia Mejor begins amid catastrophe. Lights die, people run through darkness, civilization appears to reach its conclusion, and somehow the central idea remains stubbornly hopeful. The song imagines collapse as an opening rather than merely an endpoint, asking why humanity remains frightened of change, love and the possibility of an existence radically different from the one it has built for itself. CATASTROFE CLUB can stare directly at environmental ruin, social collapse and human stupidity while maintaining an odd serenity, as though extinction might finally allow every other creature on Earth a decent night’s sleep. Musically, the group pushes further into post-rock scale and cinematic space while keeping their electronic foundation intact. Layers accumulate gradually around bass, keyboards, guitars and programming, giving the track a broad horizon without losing the dry, severe personality that has followed Herrera and Molina throughout their catalogue. Their stated influences include Sigur Rós, Idles, Fontaines D.C., Astrud and Los Punsetes, though those reference points function more like distant road signs than destinations. The accompanying video extends the song’s worldview through a montage of retrofuturist imagery, historical disorder, and footage of the duo performing. Visions of technological progress collide with reminders of twentieth-century chaos, creating the uncomfortable sensation of watching humanity repeatedly advertise tomorrow while wrecking today. Watch the video for Un dia mejor below: Tension sits at the center of UN FUTURO TRANQUILO. CATASTROFE CLUB imagines a peaceful future precisely because humanity may no longer occupy it. There is cruelty in the joke, certainly, but also a strange tenderness toward whatever survives us. For these two chroniclers of decline, a better day may still be coming. We simply might not be invited. items._cn_summary: 西班牙二人组CATASTROFE CLUB的新单曲《Un Dia Mejor》延续了他们对文明崩溃主题的冷静凝视。作品融合后朋克、暗潮、后摇与电子元素，在贝斯、键盘、吉他与编程音色之间建立宽阔的音场层次。Herrera粗粝的念白介于公共播报与哲学控诉之间，将末日叙事转化为某种奇异的平静。歌词将人类消亡视为其他生命的解脱，把崩塌视为重新开始的契机而非终点。音乐视频采用复古未来主义影像与二十世纪混乱画面交织，强化了人类反复许诺明天却摧毁今天的荒诞感。作为专辑《UN FUTURO TRANQUILO》的先行单曲，作品展示了乐队在保持电子根基的同时向更大格局的声景探索。两位成员对Sigur Rós、Idles、Fontaines D.C.等乐队的影响只是路标而非终点，作品本身保有独立而干涩的个人辨识度。

items.body: Halcyon eyes, kind of gloomy in-between (If not now, then when we gonna do it, baby?) Holy pledge, Nostradamus said we’re clean (If not you, then who is gonna teach it to me?) PONS have somehow made a song that sounds as though a demon discovered stimulants, bought an expensive string section, read half a book about Roman emperors, and immediately decided he ought to run for king of hell. IF NOT NOW… is five-plus minutes of Brooklyn dance-punk delirium built around repetition as both engine and psychological hazard. Jack Parker and company plant a krautrock riff in the floorboards, then proceed to furnish the room with strings, horns, electronic abrasion, post-punk angles, and enough manic forward motion to make stopping seem medically inadvisable. Somewhere between Suicide, Brainiac, Liars, Sextile, and Ecce Schnak, after several catastrophic decisions, PONS turn excess into an organizing principle. Parker admits that excess comes naturally. “I have a really maximalist impulse when I’m writing music that I’ve recently been trying to get away from.” You can hear him losing that argument in spectacular fashion. The Eclectica String Quartet enters the picture alongside arrangements refined with Steve La Rosa, and suddenly the song has the air of an espionage film whose secret agent has misplaced the microfilm and joined a Dionysian cult instead. The repetition is crucial. PONS keep worrying the central figure until familiarity starts producing strange side effects, with each return carrying another detail, another escalation, another reason to suspect somebody has slipped something questionable into the punch. Parker wanted “something as repetitive and hypnotic as possible,” and the band stretches that idea toward absurdity without losing its grip on the dance floor. Lyrically, appetite keeps mutating. Sex, ambition, prophecy, intoxication, history, conquest, divine entitlement, and cultural memory pile together until the speaker begins sounding less like a romantic opportunist than somebody preparing to annex a small republic before breakfast. Desire becomes destiny; destiny develops an ego problem. By the closing stretch, bravery, brutality, providence, and personal mythology have become indistinguishable enough to suggest that civilization may have been a clerical error. Animator Arturo Baston pushes the same madness into the accompanying video. “Arturo had the idea of animating some sort of nightmare carnival bumper car ride filled with freaks and ghouls,” says Parker. From there, Parker becomes a Ghost Rider-like figure traveling through the underworld on his way toward infernal royalty, because apparently ordinary professional advancement was unavailable. Watch the video for If NOT NOW… below: IF NOT NOW… belongs to the forthcoming RACECAR, out November 5 via Casa Gogol Records, Eugene Hütz’s new label. If this single represents the album’s governing philosophy, PONS have built themselves a machine whose accelerator has been welded permanently to the floor. Normies should probably stand clear. Listen to IF NOT NOW… below and order the single here. You can pre-order RACECAR here. items._cn_summary: PONS这首单曲以布鲁克林舞后朋克为底色，融合了krautrock式循环riff、弦乐四重奏与铜管编制，再叠加电子噪音和后朋克的锐利棱角，形成一种近乎失控的感官过剩。重复动机被刻意推至极限，每一轮回归都携带新的细节与情绪递进，使熟悉感逐渐异化为心理暗示。制作层面与弦乐编曲人合作，将迪奥尼索斯式的狂欢与谍战悬疑氛围并置，歌词层面则将欲望、野心、预言与征服欲层层堆叠，模糊个人神话与文明批判的边界。整体呈现出极高的编排密度和戏剧张力，配乐气质与歌曲内容互为镜像，适合偏好实验性后朋克与跨领域融合的听众。

items.body:
After the OĽUN album I reviewed enthusiastically a while back, here’s the next project, again motivated and led by violinist/fiddler/composer Ján Kružliak Jr., continuing the rapprochement, indeed embrace, between Slovakia’s traditional music and its classical music. This time it reconnects the works of classical composers who were inspired by and drew on village musics with those traditional sources and styles.
Three ensembles are involved: the Spectrum Quartett led by Kru�liak with two violins, viola and cello; Nogaband, the traditional-style quartet of fiddles, contra (chording viola) and bass that’s led by fiddler and singer Michal Noga; and the female vocal group Ulijanky, plus guest singer Simona Hulejov�.
The majority of the tracks are interpretations of works by Slovak composer Eugen Suchon (1908-1993), with others from fellow-Slovaks Ilja Zeljenka (1932-2007) and Alexander Moyzes (1906-1984), and Hungarian B�la Bart�k (1881-1945) who did a lot of his very detailed collecting of folk music in Slovakia.
In each case the sources - musicians and locations in villages across Slovakia - are credited in the notes, and these arrangements and performances reconnect with the energy and traditional vocal sound of those sources.
In no way is this an orchestra-smoothed thing; this is gutsy, brilliantly played and sung music with all the spirit, skill and technique of traditional music, from players and singers who deeply understand and inhabit it. It’s a glorious piece of work, music to luxuriate in. There’s too much richness to begin to detail, but here’s a dip into a few moments to give the flavor. The tracks all have very long titles detailing their sources, so for brevity’s sake I’ll just give track numbers.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由小提琴家兼作曲家Ján Kružliak Jr.主导，汇聚三组音乐力量——Spectrum Quartett弦乐四重奏、Nogaband传统弦乐四重奏与Ulijanky女性声乐组，共同探索古典与斯洛伐克民间音乐的深层交汇。曲目主体取材于斯洛伐克作曲家Eugen Suchoň、Ilja Zeljenka、Alexander Moyzes，以及曾在斯洛伐克大量采录民间音乐的匈牙利作曲家巴托克。编曲将古典作曲家的作品重新与乡村音乐的演奏传统、声乐风格和能量对接，每首曲目的长标题标注了民间音乐的采录来源和地点。演奏充满原真性，不做管弦乐式的润色，保留了民间音乐的精神、技巧与传统声乐质感，是一次古典与民间双向回溯的音乐实践。

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑聚焦于乌克兰战争中约两万名被俄罗斯强制带往俄罗斯的乌克兰儿童，以传统与现代原创歌曲交织的方式纪念这些被偷走的孩子。音乐以弓弦乐器为主，辅以班杜拉琴、钢琴及双陶笛等，集合加拿大与乌克兰两地音乐人共同录制。歌词取材于乌克兰民间谚语与传统仪式歌曲，如《Rusalka》取材于斯拉夫民间传说中的自然精灵，旋律时而温柔时而激烈。专辑在乌克兰与加拿大双重背景下完成创作，由乌克兰裔加拿大人Marichka与班杜拉琴手Alina Kuzma共同领衔，演绎传统歌曲的同时将其与当代议题结合，既有文化深度也有现实关怀。

items.album: L�ve L�ve - Sao Tom� & Principe sounds 70s-80s Vol. 2

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. Various Artists - L�ve L�ve (Volume1) (Review) Pedro Lima - Maguidala (Review) Ann O'aro - Bleu (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了20世纪70至80年代圣多美和普林西比群岛的Puxa音乐录音。Puxa是一种融合了多国元素的复合节奏，吸收了来自其他前葡属非洲殖民地的merengue、Kompas、Soukouss、Benga等元素，与加勒比海跨大西洋的音乐交流也有渊源。编曲层面展现出多把吉他交织缠绕的结构，主唱与和声在旋律框架中不断呼应，鼓手与吉他之间的紧张对话推动节奏持续延伸，舞者在此基础上被推至狂热。Pedro Lima领衔的乐队以闷音吉他的钩连句法为核心，Sangazuza则在贝斯与键盘退场后让鼓与吉他独立支撑律动。Africa Negra的曲目体现了现场演奏长时间铺陈的特点。作为非洲最小的国家之一，这些岛屿的音乐记录数量有限，更显得这份资料的珍贵。

items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items._cn_summary: Analog Africa 厂牌推出的第44号发行，收录了贝宁歌手 Antoine Dougbé 1977至1982年间与 Orchestre Poly-Rythmo 合作的作品。Dougbé 被誉为"魔鬼首相"，其创作根植于伏都教信仰，音乐中融合了由打击乐手 Belobi Meridjo 开创的 Cavacha 节奏——这一节奏源自他对火车节奏的提炼，后广泛传播至刚果流行乐。专辑中的曲目展现了古巴 son 影响的放克风格，合成器的铺垫与塑料质感的吉他音色相结合，勾勒出八十年代初非洲流行乐的独特面貌。相对厂牌此前推出的 Poly-Ritmo 合辑，此作更侧重于 Dougbé 作为创作者的个人印记，记录了这位创作生涯短暂但风格鲜明的音乐人与贝宁最负盛名的乐队之间的深度合作。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑延续了挪威Camilla Hole Trio对本土民谣与外部音乐传统的探索。高音萨克斯、低音提琴与鼓的爵士三重奏为基础，主唱Hole以萨克斯演绎挪威西部传统的Springleik舞曲旋律。乐评特别强调了三位成员之间角色边界模糊的特征：Kalman的低音提琴和模块合成器、Nesheim的颤音琴与鼓，不断在旋律与节奏之间转换承担，作品很快从旋律陈述滑入自由的即兴段落，乐手交替接管主旋律线。与前作将科幻合成器与传统素材结合的超脱感相比，这张专辑回归更朴素的土地语境，但依然保留了对固定角色分工和曲式结构的拒斥。三件乐器之间的色彩叠加与即兴流动是该专辑的核心特色。

items._cn_summary: Marie Davidson 与 Pearson Sound 首度合作推出单曲《Heat》，将 EBM 电子舞曲元素与较慢节奏结合，标志着两位艺术家首次在录音室中联手。歌曲附带扩展版本及 Autumns 的混音，后者定于10月30日发行。该作品延续了 Davidson 2025 年专辑《City Of Clowns》的探索路线，以工业电子质感为基底，通过较低的节奏速度营造压迫感与张力。整体制作偏向俱乐部暗黑舞曲美学，Pearson Sound 的制作介入为 Davidson 的人声注入更冷峻的工业纹理。作为一首合作单曲而非完整专辑，其艺术表达有所局限，但两位艺术家各自在电子与暗潮领域的积累使此次合作具备一定的化学反应。

items.body: Winter Sect have discovered one of goth’s better-kept secrets: graveyards can be funny places. Not funny in the sitcom sense, unless your sitcom happens to involve velvet sleeves, low fog, marble angels, and a bass player turning cemetery dirt into a dance floor, but funny in the grand old rock-and-roll sense that the concept of memento mori has always looked a little less terrifying once somebody places a wreath of backbeat on the coffin. Made up of Sister Ex alumna Claudia Neuman on bass and vocals, guitarist Anthony Piazza, keyboardist and vocalist Heather Wayward, and drummer Darryl J. Dardenne, the DC/Baltimore group have previously favored the colder end of Gothic psychedelia and glam rock. Graveyard Girl, however, loosens the corset. Funk, garage rock, indie pop and even bossa nova slip into the bloodstream, bringing a loose, easy groove beneath the song’s ’60s pop whimsy while the band keeps one boot planted firmly in post-punk soil. Neuman’s bass is responsible for the initial crime, strutting around with the casual confidence of someone who has found the liquor cabinet during a wake. Wayward’s keyboards add splashes of color around Piazza’s guitar, while Dardenne keeps the song moving with a lightness that gives its cemetery imagery room to grin. The melody has the cheeky charm of a vintage pop single, its tuneful bounce making the invitation to wander among the graves sound suspiciously like a proposition for a Sunday afternoon date. Siouxsie and the Banshees, March Violets, Strange Boutique and more hover somewhere in the family tree, although Winter Sect sound especially amused by the possibilities of their own material here. According to Wayward, that playful turn happened almost accidentally during rehearsal: “The song pretty much started with Claudia grooving out on a bass line,” she says. “It was catchy and I thought let’s do something completely different and not so serious and macabre. First the hook was discovered and we built from there. So with that funk of a groove my mind started walking. Where? Through the graveyard of course. It came together in a cool way and a little twist at the end just makes it fun.” That sense of fun carries into the video, which sends the band wandering through the necropolis in slow motion among candles, veils and fog. Somebody communes with the departed, everybody looks appropriately dressed for the occasion, and the solemn machinery of Gothic imagery gains a sly little wink. You half expect one of the headstones to start keeping time. Watch the video for Graveyard Girl below: Winter Sect began in late 2023 when California native Neuman and Piazza formed the project around feedback-heavy goth, New Wave, industrial and psychedelic influences. Mystic Twin and Haunted House followed in 2024, with Say Goodbye appearing in 2026. Graveyard Girl, taken from the forthcoming EP Offering, suggests Winter Sect have figured out that darkness becomes far more interesting when somebody remembers to leave room for mischief and a tune you can hum on the way home. Listen to Graveyard Girl below and order the single here. items._cn_summary: 本文评介冬之教派乐队新单曲《Graveyard Girl》及其MV。来自DC/Baltimore的四人组合以哥特迷幻为底色，此作却融入放克、车库摇滚、独立流行乃至巴萨诺瓦等多种元素，在后朋克的土壤上营造出轻松俏皮的律动。贝斯手Neuman的线条主导全曲走向，键盘手Wayward的键盘色彩点缀电吉他，鼓手Dardenne以轻盈节奏为墓地意象留出呼吸空间。旋律具有六十年代流行的诙谐魅力，使墓地漫步的意象听起来像是周日下午的邀约。据Wayward所述，这首作品的轻松转折源于排练中贝斯线条的即兴发展，乐队由此选择偏离严肃阴郁的方向。MV以慢动作呈现乐队穿行于墓园之中，蜡烛、面纱与雾气交织，哥特视觉语汇在此获得一丝狡黠的幽默感。文中也回顾了乐队自2023年末组建以来的发展轨迹，包括2024年发行的两张作品及即将面世的EP《Offering》。

items.excerpt: On 1 October 2026, Nachtmahr chose Poland to open the longest and largest tour in the project’s history: three consecutive club dates in Wrocław, Poznań and Warsaw, with Cygnosic and Bagger 258 joining the opening run before IMPERIVM continues further across Europe. items.body: On 1 October 2026, Nachtmahr chose Poland to open the longest and largest tour in the project’s history: three consecutive club dates in Wrocław, Poznań and Warsaw, with Cygnosic and Bagger 258 joining the opening run before IMPERIVM continues further across Europe. When Thomas Rainer and I spoke ahead of the tour, he admitted that beginning in Poland had originally been a logistical decision, but previous experience with Polish audiences made it an unexpectedly appropriate one. A new programme inevitably introduces a degree of uncertainty, and he expected the energy of the Polish crowd to remove it very quickly. Wrocław supplied a fairly emphatic confirmation. Three bands approached electronic physicality from markedly different directions, yet there was no weak transition between them. Bagger 258 worked through blunt rhythmic force, aggressive vocals and a very direct relationship with the dancefloor; Cygnosic loosened that geometry into something darker, broader and more fluid; Nachtmahr then inherited a room already fully activated and pushed it into a much less orderly state. The evening did not feel like a headliner plus obligatory support. Its construction mattered. And Wrocław really is being spoiled this autumn. The number of strong dark-electronic, industrial and gothic concerts passing through the city has reached the point where they are beginning to form a genuine season rather than a handful of unrelated bookings. This was another very persuasive addition. Bagger 258 Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil I should already have seen Bagger 258 at the NCN Warm-Up this year, but unfortunately missed them there, so Wrocław finally gave me the chance to catch up. It took very little time to understand what I had missed. The Augsburg duo, Nico von der Eisenmühle and Tim “Hacke” Schmelzer, released their debut album “Aufwärts gehts bergab” in February 2026. Its language places them firmly inside EBM: Arbeiterwut, Funktion, Kontrolle!, Werkshalle 4, “Körperkommando“, Schicht im Schacht. Machinery, work, discipline and repetitive physical action are everywhere in the imagery, while Nachtmahr themselves contributed a remix of “Werkshalle 4” to the record. Live, however, Bagger 258 were far more interesting than a catalogue of genre references might suggest. Their greatest strength was immediacy. The beats came down hard and square, the vocals had real abrasion to them, and yet the performance never became rigid. There was too much visible enjoyment onstage for that. The music was aggressive, but the aggression kept converting itself into movement. There is a considerable difference between performing the visual grammar of old-school EBM and actually making a room respond to it. Bagger 258 did the latter. The pulse was almost mechanically regular, but the communication around it was human, animated and frequently playful. They were not protecting a historical form. They were using it. For an opening band, they also did exactly what an opening band should do without ever seeming subordinate to what followed. The audience did not require a long negotiation before deciding whether it was ready to move. Bagger 258 established that physical vocabulary almost immediately, and by the end of the set the room had already shifted from people waiting for the main act into people actively participating in the evening. Rainer had told me before the tour that the right support band changes the condition in which a headliner encounters its audience. If someone else has already brought the room to a certain level, you do not have to begin from zero. Bagger 258 made the point rather convincingly. Absolute knockout. Cygnosic Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Cygnosic changed the type of pressure rather than reducing it. The Athens project of Georgios Psaroudakis has a long history within dark electro, with Psaroudakis writing, performing and producing the material himself. “Demystify”, released in 2023, was Cygnosic’s seventh full-length album, while 2025’s “Theorem” reconstructed existing Cygnosic pieces through metal arrangements and showed how naturally heavier structures can sit inside the project’s electronic identity. That breadth could be felt live. Compared with the harder edges of Bagger 258, Cygnosic sounded more fluid and spacious, but describing it simply as “gentler” would undersell what was happening. The force had merely changed direction. Instead of striking repeatedly at the centre, the arrangements seemed to spread across the room, gathering weight through layers, melody and continuity. There was more air inside the music and more room for individual elements to develop. The rhythms still carried the performance, but the relationship between rhythm and atmosphere was different. Movement became less regimented, more continuous. The set could be forceful without constantly attacking. That made Cygnosic particularly effective in the middle position. Bagger 258 had already established the body as the evening’s main point of communication; Cygnosic kept the body engaged while changing how it moved. The result was dynamic, dark and surprisingly graceful. It also prevented the three-band bill from becoming three variations on the same impact. By the time Cygnosic finished, the audience was still physically engaged but had travelled through a noticeably different emotional texture, leaving Nachtmahr with exactly the kind of room Thomas Rainer had spoken about before the tour: warmed up, responsive and ready to be pushed considerably further. Nachtmahr Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil When Thomas Rainer and I spoke for Side-Line in August, much of our conversation circled around a contradiction at the centre of Nachtmahr live. The project’s visual language is built from command, discipline, uniforms, hierarchy, severity and theatricalised authority. Producing that world requires enormous control: sound, lighting, costumes, movement, timing and musicianship all have to function together. Yet the result Nachtmahr seeks from the audience is almost the exact opposite. The crowd is invited to abandon restraint, surrender to rhythm and lose control inside something that has been very carefully controlled on its behalf. For Rainer, the construction starts with the songs themselves. As he told me then, “The setlist is the script for the movie we present every night on tour.” The first IMPERIVM show gave that sentence a much more concrete meaning. The album, released on 26 June 2026 through Trisol, develops methods Rainer had already begun testing on “Verboten!” rather than simply applying another layer of production to an established Nachtmahr template. In our interview, he described Verboten! not as the end point of an evolution but as the record that established the method for what followed. IMPERIVM takes that logic further while retaining the project’s unmistakable rhythmic and visual identity. Onstage, however, theory disappears very quickly behind physical action. Thomas Rainer commands a room in a way relatively few performers can. That is not simply another way of saying that he is charismatic. What impressed me was how actively he reads the response in front of him. A gesture produces a reaction; he catches that reaction and sends it back, larger. The next rhythmic hit strengthens it again. The relationship becomes circular rather than one-directional. In Wrocław, that feedback loop escalated with remarkable speed. The entire live formation is central to why it works. Nachtmahr no longer reads as one central figure surrounded by secondary decoration. There are several simultaneous points of attention across the stage, and the movement between them gives the performance much of its tension. The musicians maintain the structural discipline, while the women in the production are integral to the stage language rather than simply ornamental additions. Their choreography, posture and interaction reinforce Nachtmahr’s play with authority and submission. They contribute to the sense of order, but also to its deliberate instability. The more precisely the stage is arranged, the more excessive the activity in front of it can become. And the audience went completely wild. Not “wild” merely because people were dancing hard. What happened was cumulative. The room became denser at the front, hands were constantly raised, bodies moved forward, and the separation between active participants and passive spectators progressively disappeared. Every successful exchange with the stage seemed to authorise a larger response. That is why “madness” is both tempting and slightly inadequate as a description. The apparent madness had an architecture. It was being built. Rainer had explained in our interview that his band and crew remove much of the need for conscious control once he is onstage, allowing him to respond instinctively and become absorbed in the energy coming back from the room. He wanted the same for the audience: a framework reliable enough that people could safely lose themselves inside it. “I have a wonderful band and crew who take the need for control out of my hands, so I can completely let go onstage and simply become one with the energy of the crowd.” Wrocław demonstrated exactly what he meant. Bagger 258 and Cygnosic had already brought the audience a considerable distance. Nachtmahr did not have to spend the opening part of the set manufacturing involvement. They could begin by directing something already in motion. From there, the room became increasingly feral. One of the most striking aspects of a Nachtmahr show remains this gap between what the imagery appears to promise and what the live experience actually produces. Onstage there is hierarchy, command and discipline; in front of it, the effect is strangely collective. The imagery separates roles, while the music dissolves them. People move together. The stricter the construction onstage became, the less restrained the audience appeared. And in the middle of all that force came one of the evening’s most delicate moments. Thomas Rainer took time to remember Witek Kopytko, our colleague and a deeply valued member of the scene, who passed away earlier this year. He distributed tiny toy horses among people in the audience in Witek’s memory. It was a small, personal gesture, but precisely because nothing about it was inflated into spectacle, it carried real emotional weight. For those of us who knew Witek, worked alongside him or simply shared this scene with him over the years, the moment briefly changed the emotional temperature of the room. The concert had been built around movement, control and physical intensity; suddenly there was space for affection and remembrance. It was a genuinely beautiful tribute to a colleague who is very much missed. It also said something important about what these scenes actually consist of. Bands, promoters, journalists, photographers and audiences may occupy different roles at an event, but over years those roles begin to overlap into a community. Remembering one of its people in the middle of such a large production was not a detour from the evening. It belonged there. When the music resumed, the contrast only made the final part of the set more pronounced. The machinery returned, the crowd returned to movement, but the evening had briefly revealed something much softer underneath it. The setlist Rainer’s description of the setlist as dramaturgy becomes particularly interesting when looking at the stage sheet from Wrocław. New IMPERIVM material was not placed into an isolated promotional block; it sat among songs from different periods of Nachtmahr’s catalogue. With the clearly crossed-out alternatives on the photographed sheet omitted, the visible running order was: Wer Wind sät, Keine Lieder, Weil ich’s kann!, Liebst du mich?, Tanzdiktator, Stärker als ihr Hass, Sirenen, Heile mich, Die Straße, Kampfbereit, Beweg dich!, “Mädchen in Uniform“, Unterwerfung, Der Schlaf, Katharsis. Ending on “Katharsis” was especially fitting. By that stage, the idea had already been enacted physically for well over an hour. Wrocław, and what comes next There was something especially satisfying about watching all of this happen here. Wrocław has been remarkably well served by dark music this autumn, and the concentration of good bookings is beginning to change the rhythm of the city’s scene. It matters that international industrial, EBM, darkwave and gothic artists are not simply appearing as occasional exceptions but arriving regularly enough for audiences to develop continuity between events. That continuity is important because nights like this depend on difference as much as similarity. Bagger 258 took familiar EBM mechanics and made them feel immediate, aggressive and highly physical rather than nostalgic. Cygnosic widened that physicality into something more fluid, melodic and atmospheric. Nachtmahr then absorbed everything accumulated during the previous sets and used it as raw material for a performance based on reciprocal escalation. The Polish IMPERIVM opening continues with Poznań at Pod Minogą on 2 October and Warsaw at VooDoo Club on 3 October, before the tour moves on internationally. Audience in Wrocław Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil Photo: Karo Kratochwil About Nachtmahr, Cygnosic and Bagger 258 Bagger 258 are an Augsburg-based German EBM duo formed by Nico von der Eisenmühle and Tim “Hacke” Schmelzer. Their debut album “Aufwärts gehts bergab” was released in February 2026 and includes remixes by Nachtmahr, NordarR and Menticide; Side-Line covered the album in a March 2024 interview with the duo. Cygnosic is the Athens-based dark-electro project of Georgios Psaroudakis. “Demystify” appeared in 2023 as the project’s seventh full-length album, while 2025’s “Theorem” revisited Cygnosic compositions through metal arrangements without abandoning the project’s electronic core. Side-Line first covered the Nachtmahr connection in 2019, when Cygnosic toured with Nachtmahr and labelmates C-lekktor behind the “Epiphany” LP. Nachtmahr, founded by Austrian musician Thomas Rainer in 2007, has developed a distinctive language around hard electronic rhythm, theatrical authority, confrontation, discipline and increasingly broad stylistic freedom. IMPERIVM is the latest stage of that development, while the current tour is the largest and longest undertaken under the Nachtmahr name. The Wrocław opening showed how carefully the three-band construction worked: Bagger 258 established the body, Cygnosic changed the way it moved, and Nachtmahr took control of what had already been set in motion. By the end, the contradiction Thomas Rainer and I had discussed before the tour, extreme control on one side of the stage and deliberate surrender on the other, no longer needed explaining. It was visible everywhere in the room.
items._cn_summary: 本文为Nachtmahr、Cygnosic与Bagger 258三支乐队在波兰弗罗茨瓦夫联合演出的现场乐评。Nachtmahr选择波兰开启其历史上最长的大型巡演，三支乐队从不同方向切入电子音乐的肉体性。Bagger 258以直接有力的节奏冲击舞池，歌词充满机械、劳作与纪律的EBM意象；Cygnosic将几何感延展为更暗、更流动的形态；Nachtmahr在观众已被充分激活的基础上将现场推入更无序的状态。三组之间的过渡没有明显断层，编排逻辑清晰。波兰，尤其是弗罗茨瓦夫，秋季已形成密集的暗黑电子、工业与哥特演出季。评论同时提及Bagger 258 2026年首张专辑及Nachtmahr参与的混音作品，呈现该厂牌体系内部的紧密协作。

items.body: Death Strip release their fourth single, “Flash Back,” on October 8, 2026. The duo mixes darkwave and EBM with an electro-punk edge. “Flash Back” runs at 136 BPM, built on distorted saw bass, strobing arpeggios and deadpan spoken word. Recommend to fans of Boy Harsher, Gesaffelstein and The Prodigy. The single is scheduled to land on Death Strip’s Bandcamp and Spotify pages on release day. About Death Strip Death Strip pairs Jonas Moberg, a Swedish producer and drummer based on Gotland, with vocalist Culture Yob, also known as Son of Daughter, based in Hastings, England. Moberg played drums in the Swedish rock band Jumper, which released three albums and eleven singles between 1996 and 2000, and later played live drums for Paloma Faith early in her career. Culture Yob co-founded the band Gobsausage with Takalina and Miss Halski in the early 2000s, and also co-founded Charles of London, according to the band. The two met in the 2000s and lived in neighboring warehouse flats in Shoreditch, London, where they shared a goods lift. They now live apart, Moberg on Gotland and Culture Yob in Hastings, and write and record Death Strip’s music remotely. The two have never been in the same room for a Death Strip session. “Flash Back,” released October 8, 2026, is the fourth single Death Strip has made this way.
items._cn_summary: Death Strip 是一支由瑞典制作人 Jonas Moberg 与英国 vocalist Culture Yob 组成的双人组合，二人早年同住伦敦 Shoreditch 仓库公寓，现分别居于瑞典哥特兰岛与英国黑斯廷斯，以远程方式合作，从未在同一录音室共同录制。"Flash Back" 是他们以此方式制作的第四支单曲，定于10月8日发行。作品速度为136 BPM，以失真锯齿波贝斯线、频闪式琶音与冷调念白为核心，融合 darkwave 的暗黑氛围、EBM 的机械律动与 electro-punk 的粗粝锋芒。乐评将其推荐给 Boy Harsher、Gesaffelstein 与 The Prodigy 的爱好者。整体定位明确，音色设计偏向工业化与舞曲化的结合，但内容更像产品信息发布而非深度评论，对其艺术实验性的探讨较为有限。

items.body: Belgian electronic artist Franky Deblomme releases a new EP as Cubic, “Elements,” on October 2, 2026 via Alfa Matrix. The five-track digital release moves the project’s minimal electro sound into more dynamic techno territory. Elements EP by CUBIC ‘Elements’ draws on 80s electro, 90s techno and dub techno “Elements” draws on 1980s electro, 1990s techno in the style of R&S Records, and acid and dub techno, the reference points that have run through Cubic’s sound over the years, with Alfa Matrix noting a nod toward contemporary acts such as Bicep and Modeselektor. Opening track “Future Past” and the two versions of “BangBang,” a Detroit edit and a Chicago edit, push the EP toward a more dancefloor-oriented, energetic direction. “A Fish” and “Chord Memory” keep the minimal sequences, vintage electronics and repeating patterns that recur through Cubic’s releases. ‘Elements’ EP tracklist “Future Past” (4:31) “BangBang” (Detroit edit) (4:26) “A Fish” (4:35) “Chord Memory” (4:55) “BangBang” (Chicago edit) (4:10) The EP is a digital release, available as a download via the Alfa Matrix Bandcamp page, with streaming included, at up to 24-bit/44.1kHz. About Cubic Cubic is the electronic project of Belgian artist Franky Deblomme, also known for his earlier work as 808 Dot Pop. Deblomme signed Cubic to Alfa Matrix and released the project’s label debut EP, “Alphabet Hymn,” on March 9, 2021. The five-track EP combined vintage Dusseldorf synth influences, Berlin techno, 1990s Manchester rave and EBM, built entirely on hardware synthesizers and effects at Deblomme’s Bong 13 studio, and included a remix by label mates 808 Dot Pop. Later that month, Cubic reworked an earlier 808 Dot Pop album into “The Cubic Temperature,” released March 26, 2021 with an exclusive Bandcamp megamix bonus track. Cubic’s debut album, “The Cubic Alphabet,” arrived on June 18, 2021. The project continued with the EP “Phonic Lessons Part 3” on December 7, 2021, then the singles “Exit – Frankfurt” on April 7, 2022 and the four-track “Exit – Ghent” on June 29, 2022, each tied to a specific city’s electronic scene. The EPs “c64” (September 18, 2023) and “c128” (December 6, 2023), both referencing Commodore home computers, preceded the album “Back To Basic,” released on Alfa Matrix on June 4, 2024 with a Kraftwerk-indebted sound made using the first Belgian-made drum computer (Modor DR2) and synthesizer (Modor NF1). Cubic released the vinyl EP “EFM01 (Black)” in an ultra-limited run in June 2025, then the digital EP “EFM02” in October 2025 and the rework album “Back To 808” in December 2025. The twin EPs “CB-708” and “CB-128,” revisiting “Back To 808,” came out in February 2026. “Elements,” out October 2, 2026, is Cubic’s newest EP on Alfa Matrix. items._cn_summary: 比利时电子音乐人Franky Deblomme以Cubic之名在Alfa Matrix厂牌发行五曲EP《Elements》。整张作品延续了项目多年来的复古电子脉络，汲取八十年代electro、九十年代R&S厂牌风格的techno，以及acid与dub techno元素，并被厂牌拿来与Bicep和Modeselektor等当代艺人作比。部分曲目如《Future Past》和《BangBang》的底特律与芝加哥双版本编辑更趋舞曲化与能量化，而《A Fish》与《Chord Memory》则保留极简序列、复古合成器音色与循环节奏模式。作品完全在Deblomme位于比利时的硬件合成器与效果器工作室Bong 13中构建，延续了他对硬件音色的坚持。整体而言，这是一张在固定美学框架内推进的EP，融合了多种techno子类型元素。

The eight-track release previews the band’s fifteenth studio album, “The Kinematics Of Doubt,” due October 30 on the same label. items.body: Belgian EBM act Implant releases the EP “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed” on October 2, 2026 via Alfa Matrix. The eight-track release previews the band’s fifteenth studio album, “The Kinematics Of Doubt,” due October 30 on the same label. I’m Only Happy When You Bleed EP by IMPLANT ‘I’m Only Happy When You Bleed’ is the second single from ‘The Kinematics Of Doubt’ The title track is the second song revealed from “The Kinematics Of Doubt,” after lead single “Underneath The Neon Lights.” Built on a 3/4 rhythm, it pairs evolving electronic layers and a shifting pulse with lyrics centered on control, cruelty and forced submission. The EP extends the single into an eight-track release. “Information Systems” opens the record with a long-form soundscape built entirely from spoken samples about the mythology of computing. “The Insider” addresses privileged knowledge and how much of what people take as fact is actually interpretation or assumption. “Pills (in f sharp)” reworks the album track “Pills” into a different key, turning its “I want more pills” refrain into both a chant and a comment on the pursuit of quick fixes. “Underneath The Neon Lights” also appears on the EP. Three remixes of the title track close the release. New York act Crash Course In Science turns the song into a club-oriented dance track. People Theatre take it in a more melodic direction before a detuned lead takes over. Belgian label mate Aiboforcen contributes a version Alfa Matrix describes as distinctly Aiboforcen’s own while staying rooted in Implant’s sound. ‘I’m Only Happy When You Bleed’ EP tracklist “Information Systems” (3:16) “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed” (4:00) “Underneath The Neon Lights” (4:55) “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed” (Crash Course In Science remix) (4:39) “Pills (in f sharp)” (4:00) “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed” (People Theatre vein remix) (5:32) “The Insider” (4:33) “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed” (Aiboforcen remix) (4:12) The EP is a digital release, available as a download in MP3 and FLAC via the Alfa Matrix Bandcamp page, with streaming included, at up to 16-bit/44.1kHz. ‘The Kinematics Of Doubt’ follows on October 30 Side-Line previously reported on “The Kinematics Of Doubt” in Implant sets 15th album ‘The Kinematics Of Doubt’ for 30 October on Alfa Matrix. The fourteen-track album is issued on CD and digital and includes “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed” alongside “The Observer Effect,” “Underneath The Neon Lights,” “Pills,” “Civilization,” “Sanity,” “Framed,” “Transaction Failure,” “Are You Crying?,” “Talking In Your Sleep,” “Beyond The Code,” “No Apologies Required,” “On TV” and “Wounds.” Implant and Llumen launch their respective albums together on November 20, 2026 at mOtown in Sint-Joost-ten-Node, Belgium. About Implant Implant is the electro-industrial project Len Lemeire started in Belgium in 1996. The debut CD single, “Fun,” credited to Lemeire alongside Geert Machtelinck, was pressed in a numbered edition of 1,000 copies that year. The project’s catalogue spans harsh EBM, industrial dance, electro-pop and dark synth across releases including “Implantology,” “Audio Blender,” “The Productive Citizen” and the EP “Fading Away,” closing most releases with the line “Did you have your Implant today?” Implant released the free download single “The Drive” in December 2023. The twelfth studio album, “The Chaos Machines Part 1 – No More Flies On The Windscreen,” followed in May 2024. Lemeire discussed its modular-synth approach and a duet with Noemi Aurora in Implant interview: ‘Embrace chaos through the machines!’. The trilogy continued with the limited vinyl EP “The Chaos Machines Part 2 – Scratching The Surface” in September 2024 and closed with the album “Judging Sinners – The Chaos Machines Part 3” on February 7, 2025, again featuring Noemi Aurora and covered in Exclusive interview with Implant judging all those sinners. “The Kinematics Of Doubt,” Implant’s fifteenth studio album, follows on October 30, 2026. “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed,” out now as an eight-track EP, is the second single revealed from the record. items._cn_summary: 比利时电子工业计划 Implant 发行 EP《I'm Only Happy When You Bleed》，作为第十五张录音室专辑《The Kinematics Of Doubt》的第二支单曲预告，收录八首曲目。标题曲采用 3/4 节拍，电子层次不断演变，脉搏节奏持续位移，歌词围绕控制、残忍与被迫服从等议题。《Information Systems》以长篇声音景观展开，全部由关于计算神话的口语采样构成；《The Insider》探讨特权知识与认知的诠释偏差；《Pills (in f sharp)》将原曲移调重构，把反复诉求转化为对速效解药的隐喻。EP 末尾收录三首混音，分别由 Crash Course In Science、People Theatre 与 Aiboforcen 操刀，呈现俱乐部化、旋律化与工业化的不同诠释方向。该作品延续了比利时暗潮工业厂牌 Alfa Matrix 旗下典型的 EBM 语汇，在节拍实验与采样拼贴方面展现出一定的手法意识。

振付（家）と権力構造。振付を「ナンセンスなゲームのルールの恣意性」へと還元する自己批判。スペクタクルとして消費される身体からの逃走。バレエという制度が内包するダンサーのヒエラルキー、さらには訓練されたプロのダンサー／アマチュアや子ども、障害者といった出演者のヒエラルキーの解体。「ダンスとは何か」について脱構築するようなコンセプチュアルな作品を制作してきたフランスの振付家ジェローム・ベル。自身の名前をタイトルに冠した本作『ジェローム・ベル』は、約30年に渡る振付家としてのキャリアと人生を振り返り、映像を見せながら自作について解説し、創作の背後にあるダンスや社会への問いを語る、2時間のレクチャー・パフォーマンスである。また、2019年以降は、環境負荷への配慮から、ベルと彼のカンパニーは飛行機での移動を行なわず、上演地ごとに、現地のパフォーマーがその土地の言葉で演じる形を採っている。日本版では、2025年の YPAMでの上演と同様、川口隆夫が「ジェローム・ベル」として出演する。「他者による代演」というもうひとつの仕掛けについては後編で詳述し、まずは本作で語られるベルの思索の軌跡を概観してみよう。 10代後半で国立ダンス学校に進学するも、従順なダンサーの養成機関にすぎないことへの失望。「踊らない」ダンサーの演劇的な仕草で観客に感銘を与えることができるピナ・バウシュの舞台に力づけられたこと。当時の1980年代は、ミッテラン大統領の進歩的な左派政権下でダンスに対する国家的支援が拡充され、コンテンポラリー・ダンスが盛行した。海外ツアーにも多く参加し、ダンサーとして華やかな経歴だったが、親友2人をエイズで亡くし、「人生で何をやりたいのか」という問いに直面したことから、振付家になろうと決心する。 ここでベルが特異なのは、振付家になるための修行期間として、2年間、美術史、文学、哲学などの読書に専念したことだ。その際、「アート」「文学」という言葉を「ダンス」に置き換えて読む。例えば、ロラン・バルトの『零度のエクリチュール』を「零度のダンス」に置換し、「ダンス」を問い直す思考のフレームを鍛える。また、ギー・ドゥボールの『スペクタクルの社会』に触発され、消費者の目を惹きつけるためにメディアが誇張する（性的）魅力に溢れた身体表象を批評するため、ダンスの媒体（メディウム）である身体を即物的な次元で扱う。本作と同じタイトルで発表された初期作『ジェローム・ベル』（1995）では、全裸のダンサーが、初めて触るものであるかのように自分自身の皮膚をつまみ、限界を確かめるようにゆっくりと皮を伸ばすシーンが紹介される。また、衝撃的なのが、舞台のみならず、日常的な社会規範からも「身体を解放」するために、ダンサーが放尿するシーンだ。全裸のダンサーは不動のまま、身体の内部にあったものが外に放出され、重力によって落下する運動が提示される。 観客の拒絶や批評家の酷評にもめげず、ベルはさらにラディカルな創作を進めていく。代表作のひとつ『The Show Must Go On』（2001）では、スペクタクルの消費社会と振付という権力への自己批評を展開。世界的にヒットしたポップ・ソングの歌詞を「振付のスコア」と捉え、特定の歌詞が流れた時だけ、ダンサーは歌詞が指示する行為を行なう。例えば、デヴィッド・ボウイの「レッツ・ダンス」がかかると、「レッツ・ダンス」と歌われるサビの間だけ、出演者はクラブ風の踊りを繰り返すが、それ以外は棒立ちの異様な時間が続く。ポリスの「見つめていたい」が流れると、出演者は舞台前面に一列に並び、客席を黙って凝視する。高尚なダンス／ポップ・カルチャーというヒエラルキーや、「見る／見られる」の非対称性の解体と同時に、ムーブメントの審美性や高度なテクニックが排除され、「振付とは、身体に課されたゲームのルールにすぎない」という恣意性や権力性が露わになる。 また、ベルは2000年代以降、パリ・オペラ座バレエ団からの依頼（！）を契機に、ダンサー自身が実演を交えて自伝を語る「ドキュメンタリー・ポートレート」のシリーズに取り組む。アマゾンの先住民の部族をフィールドワークしたクロード・レヴィ＝ストロースの文化人類学を参照し、「バレエという未知の体系」が研究対象にされた。調査サンプルとして起用されたのが、バレリーナのヴェロニク・ドワノーだ。バレエ団のヒエラルキーでは中間に位置するドワノーは、主役のエトワールを引き立てるために舞台美術のように静止する時間が最も辛いと語り、群舞と静止を行き来するシーンを実演してみせる。『白鳥の湖』の優美な音楽が覆い隠していたのは、ダンサーを非人間的な部品に変えるバレエの階級制度と、その基盤にある国家権力（絶対王政期に設立された王立ダンスアカデミー）だ。 ［Documentation Team © 2026 Hot Summer in Kyoto］ 2010年に入ると、ベルは、知的障害者の団体から依頼され、「言葉で表現することが難しい出演者とともに、人間性を疎外せず、どう創作できるか」という困難な問いに向き合う。『The Show Must Go On』のメソッドを応用しつつ、「出演者が自分の好きな曲を選び、自身のソロを作って踊る」という委ね方を選択した。踊りに熱中する出演者たちのパワーに圧倒され、「今、ここ」を生きている身体ほど舞台においてパワフルなものはないと語るベルは、『Disabled Theater』というタイトルとは裏腹に、この作品では、振付家という特権性からの解放、社会規範を解除する場として立ち上がる舞台、そして社会で周縁化された存在に表現力という力と武器を与えるものであったと振り返る。 『Disabled Theater』は高く評価されたが、「一人ひとり違うはずなのに、知的障害者としてひとくくりにされてしまう」という反省から、車椅子ユーザー、子ども、クィア、移民、定年退職者などより多様な出演者とともに、同じ手法でつくり上げたのが『Gala』（2015）である。また、『Disabled Theater』では、中央でソロを踊る出演者を、他の出演者が椅子に座って見つめるという構造だったが、『Gala』では、ソロの踊り手の動きを真似して他の出演者も一緒に踊ることにより、ソロ／群舞という境界も流動化させた。「それぞれが個でありながらどう平等でいられるか」という複雑な方程式をダンスで解くことの喜びがあったとベルは語る。 そして、イサドラ・ダンカンの自伝を元に彼女についての伝記的な作品をつくったことを契機に、ベルは、自身について語るこの作品『ジェローム・ベル』をつくるに至ったと語る。ダンスをめぐるラディカルな思索が2時間に凝縮された本作はそれだけでも十分に面白いのだが、さらにもうひとつの仕掛けが加算される。ここまで「ベルは」という主語で述べてきたが、実際に本上演で「ジェローム・ベル」として登場するのは、本人ではなく、川口隆夫という日本人のパフォーマーが日本語で語る。直接的な契機は気候変動対策であるとベルは述べるが、「本人ではない他者が振付家の自伝を語る」という構造は、「振付」それ自体についてのさらなる問いを推し進める。それは同時に、ダンス（舞台芸術）の反復性・再現可能性や、映像アーカイブと舞台芸術の一回性の問題についても問う作業になるだろう。 鑑賞日：2026/08/05（水） 関連レビュー 越智雄磨『コンテンポラリー・ダンスの現在──ノン・ダンス以後の地平』｜高嶋慈：artscapeレビュー（2020年07月15日号） 未だ見ぬ身体へ──川口隆夫『大野一雄について』｜岡村恵子：フォーカス（2017年11月15日号） ジェローム・ベル『ザ・ショー・マスト・ゴー・オン』（The Show Must Go On）｜木村覚：artscapeレビュー（2011年12月01日号） （後編へ）※10/5公開予定
items._cn_summary: 本文为法国概念编舞家杰罗姆·贝尔同名作品的京都公演前篇乐评，深入梳理其三十年创作脉络。从早期以阅读哲学替代传统训练、将罗兰·巴特文本中「文学」替换为「舞蹈」进行思考，到《杰罗姆·贝尔》（1995）以全裸身体探讨媒介物质性；至《The Show Must Go On》将流行歌曲歌词作为编舞脚本，解构观看权力与身体规训。贝尔的「纪录片肖像」系列以巴黎歌剧院芭蕾舞团舞者为对象，揭示古典制度中的阶级与国家权力结构。后期《Disabled Theater》《Gala》则与残障人士、儿童、酷儿等多元群体合作，将编舞特权交还个体，探讨平等与差异的辩证。本次京都版由川口隆夫代为出演，文章聚焦思想轨迹的概要。

items.excerpt: 京都を拠点とするバンドの、久保田麻琴プロデュースによる3作目。鴨川に架かる橋の数え歌“鴨ノ橋”が生むサイケでディープな音の渦に飲み込まれたかと思えば、サックスが咆哮するガレージ・ロック、ブギウギ調のウィード・ソング、レイドバックしたソウル風ナンバーと続き、尋常ではないエネルギーと尖った感性が発揮されている。“鴨ノ橋”のトランシーなリミックスも強烈!

items._cn_summary: 京都乐队FRYING DUTCHMAN的第三张专辑由久保田麻琴操刀制作，呈现出多变的风格面貌。开篇曲"鴨ノ橋"以鸭川桥梁为意象营造出迷幻而深邃的音墙，随后转向萨克斯主导的车库摇滚冲击、布吉摇摆律动的迷幻歌曲，再到放克灵魂风慢板，风格跨度极大。专辑收录了"鴨ノ橋"的恍惚系remix版本，强化了迷幻听感。整体制作体现了高密度能量输出与锐利感性，但未深入触及纯实验或前卫领域，更偏向摇滚框架内的风格拼贴与迷幻探索。

items._cn_summary: 本篇乐评汇总了Marc Masters在Good Experimental Music九月专栏中对二十张发行的评述，其中包含十篇完整评论与十项补充推荐。涵盖范围涉及drone、即兴、电子与声音艺术等多个实验音乐分支，重点作品包括Cinchel的相位作品《The 4 Stages of Long Phase》、Brittany Karlson与Nick Neuburg的二重奏、Leafcutter John的《Warm Grit》以及Rob Magill的《Subtle Chaos》。作为月度发行综述，文章定位偏向信息整合与导览性质，而非对单一作品进行深度剖析。读者可借此概览当下实验音乐领域的多样动态，但若希望深入了解某张专辑的制作细节或美学脉络，仍需查阅原始评论全文。整体而言，文章适合作为实验音乐听众的选碟参考，覆盖面广但深度有限。

items.body: Absence makes the art grow bolder says Will Ainsley about Archives, which sounds like Chiastic Slide-era Autechre reimagining the Wicker Man soundtrack Archives by Vanishing Twin The idea that an album could be made piecemeal, in different countries, via the internet, would have been inconceivable forty years ago. Such technology would have seemed strange; stranger still might have been the idea that the traditional method – that is, recording a series of songs in one place during a set period of time – is far less viable these days. The logistical demands of creative practice in 2026 mean a piecemeal approach is an all-too necessary solution for many artists. Studios and practice spaces are expensive to rent. items._cn_summary: 这张专辑探讨了远程协作创作的当下意义：在不同国家通过互联网分段拼接完成录音，这一方式在四十年前难以想象，却是当下许多艺术家面对高昂录音棚租金和时间协调困难时的现实选择。文章将作品声音比作Autechre早期作品重新诠释《异教徒》电影配乐，暗示其在电子实验与迷幻氛围之间游走。专辑采用碎片化制作流程，跨越地理边界拼接而成，反映了2026年音乐人创作方式的结构性变化。声音层面融合了合成器质感与民俗式诡异氛围，介于实验电子与电影配乐式的场景感之间。制作方式本身成为作品概念的一部分，远程碎片化的录音过程映射出当代独立音乐人的生存现实。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — More than a decade after releasing the fairly experimental 'Nocturniquet', The Mars Volta returnedwith a brand-new self-titled studio album, released by Clouds Hill in 2022. A brief hiatus and asecret 2019 reunion led to the formation of an updated lineup featuring the creative core of Omarand Cedric alongside bass player Eva Gardner, drummer Willy Rodriguez and synth player MarcelRodr�guez-L�pez. In what could only be interpreted as a creative reset for the band, 'The MarsVolta' represents a bold and spiritually moving art rock collection that sees the prog innovatorsplaying a warm and melodic combination of danceable Latin rock, neo-psychedelia with electronicundertones, and straightforward indie pop/rock. Undeniably this is the most radio-friendly versionof the band so far, whereas the writing of Omar Rodr�guez-L�pez sounds grounded, smooth, andconfident, and has little in resemblance with the unhinged experimentation that had marked The MarsVolta's earliest efforts.Catchy pop tunes and eerily atmospheric indie ballads prevail here, making this release aninteresting exercise in form and texture from a band known for its exaggerated rock-basedsoundscapes. Gentle Caribbean rhythms and layered ambient sounds provide an almost psychedelicbackdrop to the album, which is quite solid overall. What each musician is playing is clearlyidentifiable, and I find that clarity valuable in an experimentally inclined pop album, although I'mnot convinced that every part of the record works equally well. While you may find extravagant andexciting accessible tunes like 'Blacklight Shine', 'No Case Gain', 'The Requisition', or 'Que DiosTe Maldiga Mi Coraz�n', 'TMV' also features a good amount of watered down and forgettable trackswith an almost complete lack of rhythmic development like 'Cerulea', 'Shore Story', and 'CollapsibleShoulders', that for me add little to no substance to the record and on certain occasions seem to bemere tracklist placeholders. It is this disbalance between excellent and bland that must havestumped most listeners upon hearing this record for the first time, including myself. And while Iappreciate the uncompromising risk the band took with this album, I ultimately have to conclude thatthis is simply not their best work.
items._genre: art rock / neo-psychedelia / Latin rock / indie pop
items._cn_summary: 这是The Mars Volta暌违多年的同名回归专辑，由Omar与Cedric核心搭档联合新阵容共同完成。专辑呈现出明显的创作转向，从早期失控式前卫实验转向温暖流畅、朗朗上口的方向，融合了加勒比节奏、电子底色与新迷幻氛围，旋律感强，被乐评视为乐队迄今最具电台亲和力的作品。编曲层次清晰，各乐器声部辨识度高，加勒比律动与环境音色构建出迷幻底色。然而专辑存在明显的质量不均衡问题：部分单曲如《Blacklight Shine》《No Case Gain》兼具感染力与结构感，而《Cerulea》《Shore Story》《Collapsible Shoulders》等曲目则被指节奏发展匮乏，更像是占位曲目。整体虽有突破舒适区的勇气，但在实验深度与旋律可听性之间的取舍尚未完全令人信服。

items.body: Review by DimitrisTheHead — Miles Davis released three albums in 1968. Nefertiti, Miles in the sky and Filles de Kilimanjaro. FdK is the least rated on this website but is my favorite out of these three records. Like any other Miles Davis album of course, this one as well is consisting of an all-star line up of musicians and that alone is a good enough reason to listen to as many as possible Davis records you can. The musicianship is always fantastic. The album kicks of really strong, and then becomes mellower yet really beautiful. The perfect epilogue before the Miles Davis electric and frantic period of jazz/rock records.

items._cn_summary: 这张1968年的专辑处于Miles Davis从后波普向电气化时期过渡的关键节点，是其进入爵士摇滚狂飙阶段前的终章。专辑开场强劲有力，随后转向更为柔和却依然动人的段落，展现了编曲上的层次递进与情绪弧线。阵容汇集了多位当时最杰出的爵士乐手，器乐演奏水准精湛。评论者认为这是1968年三张Miles Davis专辑（《Nefertiti》、《Miles in the Sky》、《Filles de Kilimanjaro》）中最为出色的一张，尽管在网站评分上偏低。整体定位为爵士融合的过渡性作品，兼具传统爵士的精致与即将到来的电气化探索。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是软机器乐队的首张作品，也是唯一一张由凯文·艾尔斯担任贝斯手的录音。乐评将其定位为1968年坎特伯雷场景中的先驱性psychedelic/progressive作品，以高超的技艺和jazz/rock/pop的融合为主要特征。艾尔斯与鼓手罗伯特·怀亚特（同时主唱）构成了强劲的节奏底座，迈克·拉特利奇的风琴演奏被描述为与同时期英国键盘手一样具有催眠般的魅力。整张专辑以即兴化的器乐编织为主线，在某些段落呈现出行进曲折、难以追随的特质，但整体的groovy律动与多元风格拼贴仍保持着对听众的吸引力。作为坎特伯雷场景的源头之一，它在爵士摇滚融合与psychedelic语汇之间开辟了一条独特的路径。
