items.excerpt: Two newly reissued albums showcase the seismic psychedelia of George Clinton’s Funkadelic at its rawest and most disruptive, writes John Morrison in The Wire 512 Funkadelic Free Your Mind And Your Ass Will Follow Westbound/Org CD/DL/LP/2xLP/MC Maggot Brain Westbound/Org CD/DL/LP/2xLP/MC Released the summer before Jimi Hendrix tragically passed away in 1970, Free Your Mind And Your Ass Will Follow was not only the follow-up to Funkadelic’s promising self-titled debut of the same year;
items.body: Two newly reissued albums showcase the seismic psychedelia of George Clinton’s Funkadelic at its rawest and most disruptive, writes John Morrison in The Wire 512 Funkadelic Free Your Mind And Your Ass Will Follow Westbound/Org CD/DL/LP/2xLP/MC Maggot Brain Westbound/Org CD/DL/LP/2xLP/MC Released the summer before Jimi Hendrix tragically passed away in 1970, Free Your Mind And Your Ass Will Follow was not only the follow-up to Funkadelic’s promising self-titled debut of the same year; it signalled the arrival of George Clinton’s ensemble as the next great voice in Black rock and psychedelia. In his 2014 memoir Brothas Be, Yo Like George, Ain’t That Funkin’ Kinda Hard On You?, Clinton acknowledges this by contrasting the album’s release with Hendrix’s death, an event that he notes as “the end of an era”. During his brief but electrifying career, Hendrix moulded multiple aspects of the Black musical tradition – blues, rock, funk, R&B, jazz – into an electrifying corpus that opened up a new world of possibilities. With Hendrix dead and the psychedelic road map that he laid out for any adventurous soul to follow, Funkadelic went on to emerge as his mightiest descendents. While Funkadelic were recording Free Your Mind Clinton absorbed and pulled inspiration from underground comics, Black power/radical leftist theory and Erich von Däniken’s work theorising that aliens had made contact with and shaped the development of ancient human civilisations. Clinton took all the disparate cultural, historical, political and extraterrestrial influences swirling around in his head and drenched them in acid. The famously LSD soaked sessions produced an album that distilled the political, cultural and philosophical DNA of the 1960s into a new musical vision for the 70s. Built around Eddie Hazel’s gnarly blues and wah-wah drenched guitar, “Funky Dollar Bill” highlights the flipside of the concept of money as freedom explored on “Friday Night, August 14th”. With lyrics like "The pusher push, the fixer fix, the judge acquits, the junkie leads his life, for the dollar bill”, it's clear that here, money is less a vehicle for freedom than a tool for control. “Eulogy And Light” serves as the perfect album closer, with Clinton praying for strength in the face of temptation and moral degradation. In an innovative display of the band's willingness to experiment with sound and concepts, the music for “Eulogy And Light” is an earlier Funkadelic track called “Open Your Eyes” spun backwards. In doing this, Clinton and crew extract the source song's optimistic heart and repurpose its gospel-inspired tune into something stranger, more twisted. Free Your Mind opens with the epic ten minute title track. Amid a ghostly mass of distorted guitar, feedback and cosmic synthesizer bleeps, Clinton screams “Free your mind and your ass will follow/The kingdom of heaven is within!”. These simple yet spine-tingling chants formed something close to a succinct mission statement. More than just slogans, Clinton was directly addressing the intellectual, physical and spiritual demands of a new musical and ideological path. He has described “Friday Night, August 14th” as a “paycheck and party song” about how a little bit of money can buy a moment of joy and freedom. In that sense, the song feels like the spiritual heir to Louis Jordan's 1949 proto-rock ’n’ roll smash “Saturday Night Fish Fry”. By the time Funkadelic entered the United Sound Systems studio in Detroit to record the follow-up to Free Your Mind, the band were at once a formidable live unit and boundless experimenters in the studio. The result of those USS sessions was 1971’s Maggot Brain, one of the greatest psychedelic rock albums ever made and the crown jewel of Clinton’s extensive body of work. The album opens with a simple and ominous message that is both a continuation of the core theme examined throughout Free Your Mind and a harbinger of the band’s future: “I have tasted the maggots in the mind of the universe/I was not offended/For I knew I had to rise above it all/Or drown in my own shit”. Here the “maggots” are the corrosive forces of ignorance, self-doubt and control that infested Free Your Mind. To all intents and purposes, Maggot Brain is a trip through the other side of enlightenment, witnessed through the prism of life, death and the liberatory potential of madness. Famously, Clinton prompted guitarist Eddie Hazel to imagine that his mother had died before recording Maggot Brain’s almost ten minute long title track. Hazel transforms his guitar into a wailing and mourning instrument of grief. Beneath his solo, a dreamy, six note arpeggio acts as the bedrock to one of the greatest guitar performances ever captured on tape. “Can You Get To That” flips the energy from dark to light with its slick groove and doo-wop harmonies. A bright and joyous song at face value, the lyrics warn that even in death, no one escapes karma. “Hit It And Quit It” is a flamboyant acid rock tune with an odd metre that betrays Funkadelic's debt to both the church and the temple of Jimi Hendrix. For an outfit that proved so adept at conjuring colourful, funky images of utopia, it's curious that they chose to close out their greatest album with “Wars Of Armageddon”. Clocking in at over nine minutes long, the song is a minefield of explosions, screams and fuzzed-out guitars. The chants of “More power to the people/More pussy to the power” offer a reminder that Funkadelic’s psychedelic ideals and ambitions never strayed too far from the funky, carnal physicality of life on Earth. This review appears in The Wire 512 along with many other reviews of new and recent records, books, films, festivals and more. To read them all, pick up a copy of the magazine in our online shop. Wire subscribers can also read the issue in our online magazine library.

items._cn_summary: 本文评介Funkadelic的两张重新发行专辑《Free Your Mind And Your Ass Will Follow》与《Maggot Brain》，聚焦George Clinton在1970年代初将迷幻摇滚、放克与黑人解放美学熔于一炉的创作脉络。文章详细描述了录音过程中LSD浸泡下的实验氛围，Clinton从地下漫画、黑豹党激进理论乃至外星人接触古文明假说中汲取灵感，将六十年代的政治、文化与哲学DNA蒸馏为七十年代的全新音乐愿景。具体音乐手法上，文章提到Eddie Hazel以wah-wah浸泡的吉他扭曲音色为核心，专辑同名开场曲长达十分钟的迷幻器乐展开，以及将早期曲目倒转处理为另一首歌的反向实验。作为Hendrix之后黑人迷幻摇滚最重要的继承者，Funkadelic在放克律动中注入酸性迷雾与宇宙意识，展现出对声音与概念的强烈实验意愿。

items.body: Los Angeles duo Patriarchy released an official video for “Lilylicker” on 29 September 2026. The track is the second song on the EP “Appendices,” released 7 August 2026 as a companion to the band’s 2025 album “Manual for Dying.” Appendices by Patriarchy The track opens on a low synth line and a steady kick drum, with Huizenga’s vocals half-whispered through the verses. The arrangement hardens into an industrial-techno beat partway through, with distorted guitars entering on the chorus. Patriarchy describes its own sound as “snuff pop,” a mix of metal, synthpop, punk and dance music. “Appendices” runs five tracks: “Bite Marks,” “Lilylicker,” “Servile,” “Ode (to an Apprehensive Tyrant)” and “Hate Fuck.” Huizenga and English wrote, performed, produced and recorded all five themselves. AJ English mixed “Lilylicker” and Enyang Urbiks mastered it. Witch Club Satan adds backing vocals on “Servile.” The EP is also out as a limited 12-inch clear vinyl edition of 300 copies, shipping around 1 November 2026, alongside digital formats on Bandcamp and streaming services. Patriarchy’s video for ‘Lilylicker’ Patriarchy directed the “Lilylicker” video itself, with cinematography by Hazel Hill McCarthy. Huizenga appears in a white gown holding lilies, then in a pink dress with chains and a metallic corset with gold wings; AJ English, also known as The Drummer, holds a skull and wears white wings. Huizenga’s son also appears in the video. The crew had to relocate the shoot outdoors to the hills above Los Angeles after the original studio balked at the concept and at having a child on set. Huizenga said the move improved the result: “A lot of the things that went ‘wrong’ ultimately added to the beauty of it, like having to shoot outside, where moths kept flying in front of our lenses.” On the project’s name and intent, Huizenga commented: “Patriarchy has never been about perfection, it’s about realizing we are the last remnants of human existence before AI enslaves us all; that’s why the project is called Patriarchy after all.” About Patriarchy Patriarchy formed in Los Angeles as a collaboration between Actually Huizenga and Andrew Means, who met when his band 3TEETH played a show at Das Bunker and offered to work with her in the studio between tour dates. Huizenga had been focused on filmmaking after a prior solo album, “Predator Romantic,” but the sessions with Means led the two to release the songs and build a band around them. Patriarchy released its debut album, “Asking for It,” on 8 November 2019 through Dero Arcade. The band built on that start with “The Unself,” released 26 August 2022, and “Manual for Dying,” out 19 September 2025 and trailed by the singles “Boy on a Leash,” “New Way” and “Die Like Everyone Else.” Patriarchy’s current lineup pairs Huizenga with AJ English, known as The Drummer. The band’s videos, including the earlier live performance clip “No Touch Torture,” are staged and directed largely by Huizenga herself. “Appendices,” the band’s companion EP to “Manual for Dying,” draws on Oscar Wilde, the Marchesa Luisa Casati, the emperor Tiberius and the Manson family as reference points. “Lilylicker” is the second single pulled from that EP, following “Servile,” and its video is Patriarchy’s newest visual release.
items._cn_summary: Patriarchy 是来自洛杉矶的双人组合，自称"snuff pop"，将金属、合成器流行、朋克与舞曲混合在一起。EP《Appendices》共五首曲目，制作由两位成员独立完成，融合低频合成器线条、工业电子节奏与失真吉他，编排从低音细语渐变为硬朗的工业-techno节拍。MV部分在洛杉矶郊外的山丘拍摄，因原定片场拒绝拍摄理念而临时转场，意外加入了飞蛾闯入镜头等即兴元素。主创 Huizenga 将项目视为人类在人工智能控制之前的最后发声，歌词与视觉围绕束缚、仪式感与反乌托邦意象展开。整体呈现出一种粗糙且带有挑衅意味的地下工业美学，与主流制作保持距离，但在实验深度上偏向类型融合而非声音探索。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是长期参与嘻哈与R&B幕后制作的多面手的首张领衔作品，作者以自身成长经历为线索，回顾了在另类音乐品味与社会对黑人音乐固有印象之间的夹缝中度过的少年时代。制作层面大量引入摇滚、爵士与非洲音乐元素，借助复合节奏构建出非常规的节拍框架，打破了类型之间的壁垒。客座阵容包括肯德里克·拉马尔、维恩斯·斯泰普斯、杰西·博伊金斯三世等当代另类R&B与嘻哈圈的重要名字，整体呈现出与主流R&B拉开距离的实验取向。专辑在主题上具有自传式的内省深度，文本层面探讨身份与期待之间的张力。评论本身偏短，提供的细节有限，但已勾勒出作品的核心美学方向。

items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. Find the artist online. Sara Serpa - Encounters and Collisions (Review) Karine Polwart- Laws of Motion (Review) Live in the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, 2025
items.label: Hudson Records
items._cn_summary: 《Windblown》源自Karine Polwart与声音设计师Pippa Murphy在爱丁堡皇家植物园的驻留项目，以园中一株2021年倒下的萨巴尔棕榈树为叙事核心。专辑以钢琴（Dave Milligan）与人声为主干，辅以精巧的声音设计构成氛围层，整体克制而内省。开篇曲《Hear The Rigging/Last In Line》旋律缓慢哀婉，颇具风笛气质，体现出苏格兰民间音乐根脉。文字与音乐中反复出现的短语成为记忆锚点，让每首歌如同一次呼吸、一段追忆。专辑虽编配简约，却在历史、自然与人类情感之间展开史诗般的凝视，Polwart温暖而富有同理心的嗓音将听者拉入旅程之中。结尾揭示了一个反讽——这棵两百年来被认定为百慕大萨巴尔的古树实为墨西哥萨巴尔——而新苗将延续它的生命，赋予这张专辑、植物与音乐共同的时间哲学。

items.body:
Though this recording documents the work of thirteen of Belgium's most innovative ensembles, the real star is the Park Abbey located just outside Leuven and founded in 1129. Built and maintained for the purpose of quiet meditation, the abbey hosted the musicians who used the quiet surroundings to prepare and record their unique musical imaginings. The result is a mostly instrumental collection that mines the riches of Belgian folk and world music traditions, including Romani scales,
La Pump
rhythms, and accordion-based
bal-musette
flavors.
For example, Slovenian-native R�n�lius Bikar�s searing violin opens the set with �R�fuge.� He and his self-named ensemble channel pan-European Roma history.
Meanwhile, �Poor Boy� is a Django Reinhardt-inspired swing tune by Charlotte Pelgen & Bipolar Bows. Pelgen sings in English, and with her ukulele strumming sounding very much like a tenor banjo, the tune is enlivened by Lotte Remmen�s St�phane Grappelli-like fiddle lines.
The distinctive sound of the oud announces yet another musical tradition. Blending Mediterranean with Arabic sounds, the Lebanese-Belgian singer Amber Haddad and her trio, oudist Adil Benhsain and double bassist Martijn Vanbuel, spin a beguiling musical web. According to the liner notes (translated from the Dutch), �Tawazden� is about �seeking balance and finding peace within a complex environment.� Further, �the various spaces of the abbey and their murals are the direct source of inspiration.�
The accordion is especially prominent. So too is the Western classical tradition. Sounding almost Baroque, �Sacristia Invisibilis,� is another standout for me. Here, mandolinist Andries Boone is joined by Anouk Sanczuk on octave violin (sometimes called the baritone violin, tuned an octave lower than standard) and on harpsichord Sandra Van der Gucht. They create an indescribable sound you have to hear.
Throughout, the Abbey�s stone presence looms. Aur�lie Charneux�s solo clarinet piece �L'Ape Millenaria� is about a thousand-year-old bee that haunts the abbey. �Thila,� by Enara Navaira, evokes ancient Celts with a jazzy double bass and drum kit behind throat singing and Citera (a kind of Hungarian zither).
Airboxes is a duo who mix chromatic and diatonic accordions. Their offering �Abdij 1� sounds improvised. Again from the liner notes, �they share their impressions of the timelessness of monastic life.�
Despite the wide range of styles,
The Sound of the Abbey
has a coherence, perhaps informed by the artists� shared inspiration. The record is often surprising and always soothing. Three years in the making, the ensembles were lovingly recorded and mixed by Bert Huysentruyt and mastered by Pieter De Wagter from Equus Mastering. They have rendered a warm sound using the natural reverb of ancient stone provided by the project�s silent partner.

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了十三支比利时创新乐团，以鲁汶郊外1129年创建的帕克修道院为录音场地，利用古老石质建筑的自然混响，呈现比利时民间与世界音乐传统的交汇。曲目涵盖罗马尼亚罗姆历史主题的弓弦作品、乌德琴与低音提琴编织的地中海与阿拉伯声音网络、文艺复兴气息的巴洛克风格曼陀林与羽管键琴组合，以及口弦琴与喉咙演唱结合的凯尔特意象。整体在修道院意象与宗教冥想氛围下保持内在一致性，录音历时三年，由Bert Huysentruyt精心混音，制作温暖而富有空间感。这是一张跨越民俗、前古典与即兴元素的跨界合辑，适合喜欢欧洲非主流音乐场景与世界音乐融合的听众。

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以墨西哥牛仔与夏威夷牧场主的历史联系为概念，将墨西哥民谣、夏威夷传统音乐和美国民谣编织在一起，十六首曲目涵盖西班牙语与夏威夷语交叉填词的新旧歌曲。核心乐器包括尤克里里、墨西哥竖琴、手风琴与滑棒吉他，编曲密集而协调。客座音乐人Taj Mahal与David Hidalgo提供了演唱与演奏的主导力量，联合多位夏威原住民歌手与团体成员共同演绎。制作以五天内一间房间的现场同期录音为主，呈现出即兴与自发性。作品体现了语言、文化、年龄与性别层面的多元合作，将两地的音乐传统以新的方式重新连接。

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. More to hear: United States of Alchemy - Songs of Compassion (Review) Dani Jan� - Vida (Review)

items._cn_summary: Alison Cotton 的新专辑《The Gods Laugh》延续了她标志性的模糊跨界风格，融合民谣、前卫音乐与宗教仪式感。乐器以中提琴、管风琴、击弦古钢琴和钢琴为主，新增鼓、贝斯与合成器层次。多数曲目为即兴演奏一气呵成，营造出穿越时空的静谧神秘氛围。专辑是 Cotton 对 2024 年底去世父亲的悼念之作，弥漫着深沉的失落感，尤其是《The Final Harvest》以她父亲最后一次造访心爱的菜园为主题，饱含难以言喻的柔情。中心曲《Sprigs of Heather》从中世纪圣咏式开篇过渡为缓慢倾泻的钢琴旋律，是一颗小巧完美的珍珠。整张专辑明暗交织、情绪流转，无法被简单归类，仅以 Cotton 之名定义便已足够。

as part of the
Prism Quartet
's new series of collaborations called
Unlocking Your Inner Composer
. If you have listened to my radio programs, you are probably familiar with the quartet's ground-breaking, genre-blurring music. If not, there's no better introduction than this.

items._cn_summary: 这张作品由David Dzubinski作曲，作为Prism Quartet「Unlocking Your Inner Composer」合作系列的一部分。作品于2025年11月在费城自由图书馆首演，邀来诗人Ursula Rucker、打击乐手Tyshawn Sorey与小提琴手Carlos Santiago共同参与编排与演绎。整首作品时长不足四分钟，却在粗粝与抒情之间反复游走，展现出细腻的技巧与充沛的能量。Prism Quartet以其打破流派边界的演奏风格著称，此作延续了这一传统，将当代室内乐写作、即兴演奏与人声朗诵融为一体，是了解该四重奏美学理念的一份良好入口。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自丹麦三人组合GuldGanger的数字EP，五首作品以传统北欧民谣为底色。主唱Mia Guldhammer嗓音成熟而有说服力，乐手各自带来不同视角。开场曲《Svennedal》以粗犷的小跑节奏展现人声魅力；唯一的原创曲目《Nordgård》由乐队成员Morten Musicus创作，口簧与风笛形成持续推进力；《Agnete Of Bjergmanden》借助扬琴营造精致背景，柔化的人声口簧增添层次；终曲《Ormsø》作为器乐曲融合长笛、弦乐与口簧，产生令人兴奋的失衡感。整张作品呈现古老而略带粗粝的氛围，乐队虽为初登场却已显得相当成熟。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / documentary audio / experimental
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑并非传统意义上的音乐作品，而是由录音师Ian Brennan在芝加哥南区街头采集的真实录音合集。二十五位枪支暴力幸存者参与了录制，年龄从十七岁到六十七岁不等，地点选在一栋九十四岁老人住宅的前廊，邻近中途机场降落航道之下。录音捕捉了社区居民讲述暴力经历的片段，包括一位老人失去两个儿子后反复道歉的场景，以及背景中街头蚊虫与环境的声响。项目收益将捐赠给致力于以公共卫生方法终结暴力的Cure Violence Global组织。作为声音文献，它跨越了音乐、社会学与人类学的边界，以极简的现场录音形式呈现了被遗忘的芝加哥南区的真实声音景观。

items.body: Review by Lewian — It is somewhat frustrating about rock from the old communist GDR (East Germany) that the possibilityof censorship didn't only affect the lyrics but apparently also had an impact on the music itself.People were strongly discouraged to think outside the box, and also to sound outside the box. Soproper innovation was very hard to find if at all. Everyone apparently wanted to (or had to) soundnice and civilised. In the 70s it was possible to play harder rock music if it clearly referenced,copied or covered rock'n roll and blues from the west as this was seen as anti western establishmentrebellion and therefore OK (at least at a certain time point), but rebellion against the ownconditions of life in the east wasn't allowed. This also meant that anything more aggressive anddark couldn't be done in innovative ways and couldn't directly relate to the musicians' daily life,seriously affecting creativity. Any opposition had to be subtle, often covered by nice melodicmusic, often enough straight and easy to listen to, and often of little attraction to the proglistener 40 years or so later. Lyrics were often poetic and indirect. Innovation could be brought in best by incorporating classical musicinfluences, as Electra and Stern Meissen did, and Lift to some extent. I believe that the situationfor creativity was really more problematic in the GDR than it was for example in Poland, Hungary andthe Czech Republic, but I can't know for sure (certainly there was a more lively jazz scene in thelatter countries).Lift's Meeresfahrt is one of the best albums to negotiate these conditions. It is in factastonishing that the major theme of longing for travel and far away countries on this album didn'tcreate problems with the censors, as far as I know, given that most people were not allowed totravel outside the eastern communist block of countries. The album is very melodic indeed, the band doesn't rock hard (OK a little bit in very few places),but they are good at what they do. Most arrangements are dominated by the two very good keyboarders.The vocals are also attractive, clean and melodic. The opener "Wir fahrn uebers Meer" is an exampleof copying western blues rock. Maybe the band used this to distract the censors, because in my viewit is by far the weakest track. This is followed by the extremely beautiful "Nach Sueden" ("GoSouth"). Not the proggiest track, but featuring a wonderful melody, a strong keyboard part, andlyrics on migrating birds that probably expressed the longing of many young people in the GDR butwere seemingly (and surprisingly) innocent enough for the censors to let the band get away withthis. A highlight!"Scherbenglas" is an example for the classical influence, using only a string section and voice. Norock at all but interesting and not bad. "Tagesreise" has an epic melody and works well asrecommendation piece for the prog fan with some contrasts and several sections. The second highlightof the album.On the B-side, "Meeresfahrt" (something like "Journey at Sea") is the longest track. It developsslowly from calm keyboards into a mostly instrumental journey featuring the keyboarders andsaxophonist in particular. This is surely enjoyable even though it may be a bit too long for what itis. "Sommernacht" is a calm good night song referencing traditional singing. It works well asending, even though not very interesting from the instrumental point of view. "Tagesreise" and "Meeresfahrt" hold most interest from the prog point of view, but the album hasvery nice elements also elsewhere if you are into melodic rock. It has light influences fromclassical music, jazz and blues. It has good variety but also comes over as consistent featuring acharacteristic style, particularly the melodies and keyboards. The most similar band I can think of is Novalis. Personally I'd rank this as thesecond best GDR prog/art rock album (after Stern Meissen's Reise zum Mittelpunkt des Menschen). 3.7stars.Sadly, few months after the release of this album in 1978, band members Henry Pacholski and GerhardZachar died in a traffic accident and the band would never be the same anymore.

items._cn_summary: 这张1978年东德乐队LIFT的专辑《Meeresfahrt》在审查严格的社会环境下创作，以含蓄方式表达对远方的向往。专辑以旋律性为核心，双键盘手主导编曲，融合了西方布鲁斯摇滚的开场与古典音乐影响。歌曲多以诗意歌词呈现迁徙鸟类等意象来隐喻年轻人的渴望，其中《Nach Sueden》以优美旋律见长，《Scherbenglas》采用纯弦乐与人声配置探索古典化表达，《Tagesreise》则展现了多段落对比的史诗性。乐评指出由于创作环境的限制，作品在创新性上有所妥协，但作为特定历史条件下东德前卫摇滚的代表作仍值得关注。整体而言对偏好实验与即兴的听众吸引力有限。

items.body: Review by Warthur — This is Jack Bruce's firet solo album, at least in terms of release date - the Things We Like jamsession was recorded prior to this and released as a follow-up. I've never fully gotten onboard withCream, and maybe it's Eric Clapton that's the component that doesn't quite land for me, becausebetween Ginger Baker's work elsewhere and now this I can say I'm more impressed with the other Creammembers' solo fare than Clapton's.What you get here is bluesy art rock with brilliant bass lines and poetic lyrics by Pete Brown. Somesongs on here ended up travelling widely, with Mountain, Colosseum, and Greenslade covering farelike Theme From An Imaginary Western or Rope Ladder To the Moon; others definitely qualify as deepcuts. Either way, well worth exploring.

items.body: Tangent Strategy announces “Tristesse”, the project’s first new full-length album in five years. The album is inspired by the music of John Foxx and Die Form. “Tristesse” explores the fragile human psyche, where anger and melancholy sit next to each other. It looks at the defiance inside relationships, healthy and unhealthy alike, and the marks they leave on the people in them. Production-wise, the album takes a simpler approach than before, keeping the songs raw with deep bass, stark arrangements and noise running through the mix. “In an age of detachment, Tristesse is a reminder that attachment is no certain comfort either,” the project states. Tristesse by Tangent Strategy About Tangent Strategy Tangent Strategy was formed in 1996 by chd.y as an outlet for a musical outlook that grew more and more drawn to industrial music over the years. The project’s first full-length, “Revenant”, came out in November 2021 via EK Product. Since then, chd.y has released several EPs under the name and performed live in Tokyo. “Tristesse”, announced in 2026, is Tangent Strategy’s second full-length album.
items._cn_summary: 这是Tangent Strategy项目时隔五年推出的第二张全长专辑，灵感来源于John Foxx与Die Form的音乐传统。专辑以脆弱的人类心理为核心议题，探讨愤怒与忧郁并存的状态，并审视其中健康与否的关系及其留下的印记。制作上转向更为简化的路径：保留低沉的贝斯线条、克制的配器骨架，并让噪音贯穿混音之中，使作品呈现出粗糙而直接的质感。专辑陈述指出，在一个疏离的时代里，执着依附同样无法提供确定的安慰，这成为整体情绪与聆听完的注解。项目自1996年由chd.y创立，首张专辑《Revenant》于2021年发行，第二张专辑《Tristesse》于2026年宣布面世。

items.excerpt: Sevit released “Requiem”, a darkwave album the Dallas-area duo wrote as the follow-up to 2021’s “On The Edge Of A Darker Place,” on 1 October 2026. The nine-track record sat unfinished for years, surfacing only after a self-titled Sevit album filled the gap in 2024. “Requiem” runs nine tracks: Ode To A Requiem Beyond My Control Escape Dreamland In So Many Words It Must Be Berlin Until Sundown The Happy Crowd The Walls Are Closing In (Original Version) Re
items.body: Sevit released “Requiem”, a darkwave album the Dallas-area duo wrote as the follow-up to 2021’s “On The Edge Of A Darker Place,” on 1 October 2026. The nine-track record sat unfinished for years, surfacing only after a self-titled Sevit album filled the gap in 2024. “Requiem” runs nine tracks: Ode To A Requiem Beyond My Control Escape Dreamland In So Many Words It Must Be Berlin Until Sundown The Happy Crowd The Walls Are Closing In (Original Version) Requiem Requiem by Sevit Sevit have not detailed why the record was set aside, but the band summed up the gap in one line: “Maybe some records simply have to wait until the people who created them finally catch up with them.” Sevit’s ‘Requiem’ follows ‘On The Edge Of A Darker Place’ “Requiem” is out now on Bandcamp as a digital release. About Sevit Jackie Legos (vocals, guitar) and Cam B. (synths, programming) write and record Sevit from the Dallas, Texas area, where the duo formed in 2020 after both had played in earlier North Texas bands, including At Night and Pleasure Crisis. They issued the “A Darker Place” EP that same year and signed to Peru’s InClub Records that October. Sevit’s debut album, “On The Edge Of A Darker Place,” arrived in September 2021: thirteen tracks that draw on The Cure, Joy Division, Bauhaus and Siouxsie & The Banshees, played live by a five-piece band built around the Legos and Cam B. core. Jackie Legos has described the band’s lyrics as rooted in “poetry, and things that might have directly and indirectly crossed my path in life.” The duo wrote “Requiem” as that album’s direct sequel, then set it aside. A self-titled album filled the gap in 2024. “Requiem” finally surfaces, closing a chapter the band had otherwise left open.
items._cn_summary: Sevit是一支来自达拉斯地区的二人组合，2026年10月1日发行了《Requiem》这张暗潮专辑，作为2021年《On The Edge Of A Darker Place》的直接续作。专辑共九首曲目，此前搁置多年，直到2024年一张自命名专辑填补空缺后才得以面世。乐队由Jackie Legos（人声、吉他）和Cam B.（合成器、编程）组成，深受The Cure、Joy Division、Bauhaus和Siouxsie & The Banshees等后朋克与哥特经典影响，以五件式编制现场演出。Legos的歌词根植于个人经历与诗歌表达。《Requiem》以数字形式在Bandcamp发行，由秘鲁独立厂牌InClub Records发行。整体而言，这是一张在暗潮/后朋克传统框架内的作品，音乐风格偏向经典致敬，文字内容以新闻报道为主，缺乏对声音设计或艺术创新性的深入评述。

items.body: The Pixel Rain released “Glitching Sky” on October 2, 2026, the fourth and final advance single from the Southeast London act’s debut album, “A Sense of Danger,” due October 29 on Bandcamp, Spotify and other digital platforms. The track pushes vocalist and multi-instrumentalist Áron Siegler’s electronic side further forward, bringing futurepop and synthwave into the project’s established synthpop sound, with Siegler citing VNV Nation and Chvrches among the single’s reference points. At the center of the song is a character retreating from an unfulfilling reality into a virtual world where he can construct a more powerful version of himself. Siegler extends the idea beyond any specific technology or platform to a broader comment on how people seek distraction from anxiety, disappointment and everyday life. Siegler describes the retreat as carrying both sadness and absurdity: “The idea came from thinking about someone whose real life isn’t giving them very much, so they retreat into a virtual world where they can be whoever they want to be. There’s something quite sad about that, but also something a little ridiculous, so I wanted the story to have both sides to it. “I deliberately left the virtual world undefined because I think that kind of escape can take a lot of different forms. I’m certainly not outside of it myself. We all have things we disappear into when reality gets uncomfortable. “The music is quite fast and energetic, but the song itself takes its time building. That seemed to fit the idea: you don’t necessarily notice yourself getting drawn further and further into these little distractions until they’ve started taking up much more of your life than you intended.” The single arrives with a visualizer by Sophie Maria Vickers, built around the song’s virtual setting and digital imagery. Glitching Sky by The Pixel Rain On Bandcamp, “Glitching Sky” is bundled together with The Pixel Rain’s three earlier advance singles, “Last,” “A Sense of Danger” and “Sacrifice.” The single is also on Spotify and other major platforms. About The Pixel Rain The Pixel Rain is the solo project of vocalist and multi-instrumentalist Áron Siegler, originally from Hungary and now based in Southeast London. The project emerged from London’s underground scene with a self-titled debut EP in 2023, and mixes dark electronic and post-punk elements with guitar, electronics and industrial textures. The Pixel Rain released the first single from its forthcoming debut album, “Last,” on June 19, 2026, with a video shot in Hungary in which Siegler was joined on screen by Balázs Fűr, András Melles, Máté Breier and Máté Király-Gyeőry. The singles “A Sense of Danger” and “Sacrifice” followed over the summer, each previewing the album further. “Glitching Sky,” released October 2, 2026, is the fourth and final advance single before the debut album “A Sense of Danger” arrives on October 29, 2026. The album explores power, authority, consumerism and social unease through recurring post-apocalyptic and technological imagery.

The track is the Bern-based darkwave, synthpop and coldwave act’s first release on the Danish label. “Last Night On Earth” follows a narrator watching Earth’s final hours from roughly seven hundred miles above the planet, aboard a spacecraft where the oxygen cycles mechanically and the view of the dying world shrinks to a reflec
items.body: Town And Towers Records has signed Swiss duo CØLDSTAR, releasing the band’s new single “Last Night On Earth” on 2 October 2026. The track is the Bern-based darkwave, synthpop and coldwave act’s first release on the Danish label. “Last Night On Earth” follows a narrator watching Earth’s final hours from roughly seven hundred miles above the planet, aboard a spacecraft where the oxygen cycles mechanically and the view of the dying world shrinks to a reflection in glass. The lyrics state the moment directly: “The blue marble fades in a rear view of glass / I watch from the silence as centuries pass.” There is no rescue attempt in the story and no final message, only “a velvet curtain, and we’re not coming back.” Dark synth layers, pulsing electronic rhythms and melancholic melodies carry the track’s icy, futuristic atmosphere. Town And Towers names VNV Nation and Black Nail Cabaret as reference points for that sound. Recommend to fans of Solar Fake, Final Selection, Depeche Mode, Covenant and The Soft Moon. CØLDSTAR’s ‘Last Night On Earth’ is the duo’s first release for Town And Towers Records “Last Night On Earth” is out now as a digital single, also streaming via Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer, Amazon Music, YouTube Music, SoundCloud and Tidal. Last Night On Earth by CØLDSTAR Town And Towers Records’ recent roster also includes deZeption, signed in 2024, and Hatif, whose album “Small States” arrived via the label in 2025. About CØLDSTAR Martin Baumann and Michael Freund record as CØLDSTAR from Bern, Switzerland, mixing darkwave, synthpop, coldwave and retro-futurist synth sounds. The duo’s songs use space and science-fiction imagery to address isolation, memory, technology, longing and human existence. CØLDSTAR’s early releases included a 2021 cover of Nine Inch Nails‘ “Hurt.” The band built out its own catalogue with the “Coming Home” EP in 2023, then the debut album “CØSMIC DUST” in 2024 via Swiss Dark Nights, combining atmospheric electronics, synthpop melody and darker post-punk influences. Singles “Time Machine,” “Astronaut’s Lament,” “Last Dance” and “Post-Punk Robot” followed. “Post-Punk Robot” reached number 2 on the Deutsche Alternative Charts in 2026. “Last Night On Earth” is the fifth single CØLDSTAR has issued since “CØSMIC DUST,” and the first through Town And Towers Records.

items.body: What’s old is always new again. We got a full-blown nü metal revival on our hands, noise rock is arguably as popular as it’s ever been, and Myspace-era metalcore is getting about as many new releases from bands with members who were born around the same time the legends were laying the foundation. I was also recently reminded that fucking Greta Van Fleet exists for some godforsaken reason. For some other reason, I feel like we’ve just kinda skipped over a lot of good stuff. Where’s the grunge revival? Where’s the college-rock revival? Where’s the early post-punk revival? Where’s all the shit that sounds like it was made by people who hadn’t yet figured out what genre they were supposed to be in? Why does everyone nowadays sound so ready to be categorized?Well, Whippets make a case to step into these shoes, sounding something like Unwound by way of Dinosaur Jr. and Jay Reatard, or like Fugazi covering Dismemberment Plan and Siouxsie and the Banshees at the same time. They convey this volatile energy with writhing guitar leads that are often as eerie as they are anthemic, and tuneful bass in a rhythm section that paves the way for both their most unruly and airy moments. Much like their 2024 self-titled release, Whippets again flex their knack for melodies that get their hooks in your eardrums like velcro. No Skulls is every bit as fearless and without boundaries, gaining traction across a multitude of late 80s and early 90s soundscapes, regularly finding familiar touchpoints with the intuition to pull the rug at just the right time, or mix ‘n’ match influences in a way that’s as much “Aha!” as it is “What the fuck?” It’s like post-punk found the perfectly imperfect dancing partner in shoegaze, distraught while still finding an endearing footing, abrasive, oddly charming, and eyebrow-raising all at once.The video for album opener “These Woods” taps into a similar throwback, like it could’ve been dug out of a shoebox full of forgotten tapes and old zines. With a hazy camcorder look, sunbleached and spliced together with live footage, BMXers, scrapbook imagery, and other ’90s feels, it has the scrappy and surreal feel of something you might’ve stumbled across on MTV’s 120 Minutes at 1 a.m. It’s an appropriate visual companion, familiar enough to trigger a deeply buried memory, but weird enough to feel like you’ve never quite seen it before—and maybe even inspire a bad haircut.Check it out: No Skulls drops today, October 2, on wax and digital via No Coast Records.

items._cn_summary: Whippets 乐队的新专辑《No Skulls》呈现出对后朋克与垃圾摇滚时代美学的致敬。乐评将其与 Unwound、Dinosaur Jr.、Fugazi 等乐队进行类比，强调吉他线条在诡异与激昂之间的张力，贝斯旋律性突出，节奏组在混乱与轻盈之间切换自如。整张专辑跨越多个80年代末至90年代初的声音景观，既有熟悉的触点，又会在意想不到的时刻抽离或混搭影响，形成既粗糙又迷人的听觉体验。首支单曲《These Woods》的MV采用90年代家用摄像机的质感，叠加阳光褪色、BMX影像与剪贴簿拼贴，呼应了MTV《120 Minutes》时代那种地下而超现实的视觉氛围。整体上，这是一张跨越多类型边界的复古致敬之作，融合后朋克的棱角与自赏派的迷离，但缺乏更深层的实验突破。

items.album: VOLKER KRIEGEL Mild Maniac (Jazz Rock/Fusion, 1974)
items.excerpt: Review by BrufordFreak — Apparently Jazz-Rock Fusion guitarist Volker Kriegel was paying close attention to the sudden rise of Power Fusion "super groups" popping up around the Jazz-Rock Fusion world (including Tony Williams' Lifetime, Jack DeJohnette's Complex, Chris Hinze's Combination, Klaus Doldinger's Passport, Brian Auger's Oblivion Express, John McLaughlin's Mahavishnu Orchestra, Chick Corea's Return To Forever, Joe Zawinul's Weather Report, Michal Urbaniak's Fusion, Herbie Hancock'
items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — Apparently Jazz-Rock Fusion guitarist Volker Kriegel was paying close attention to the sudden rise of Power Fusion "super groups" popping up around the Jazz-Rock Fusion world (including Tony Williams' Lifetime, Jack DeJohnette's Complex, Chris Hinze's Combination, Klaus Doldinger's Passport, Brian Auger's Oblivion Express, John McLaughlin's Mahavishnu Orchestra, Chick Corea's Return To Forever, Joe Zawinul's Weather Report, Michal Urbaniak's Fusion, Herbie Hancock's Headhunters, Clive Stevens' Atmospheres, Larry Coryell's Eleventh House, and, soon to come, Todd Rundgren's Utopia, Larry Young's Fuel, Tom Scott's L.A. Express, Jack DeJohnette's Direction(s), John Abercrombie's Gateway, and Stomu Yamash'ta's Go) for he decided to tag the "Spectrum" label onto this album project to connote and honor the foursome of exceptional collaborators he found to help him achieve the high standards of musicianship necessary to pull off his increasingly complex and demanding compositions. This collection of Volker Kriegel original compositions was recorded and mixed at Studio Waldorf in Frankfurt, Deutschland, between February 18 and 23, 1974, and then released by MPS Records sometime in 1974. Knowing MPS' recording-to-release turn-around patterns from the era (as well as Volker Kriegel's status as a recognized and established recording artist), I think it safe to estimate that Mild Maniac would likely have been released in the Spring of 1974.A1. "Mindwill" (6:45) some super-funky bass is joined/doubled by a second deep-funky bass, stinky funk drumming and low volume guitar, keys, and percussion as the song opens and the motif establishes itself. Effected guitar and super-funky electric piano move forward as a three-note vocal-like melody line seems to loop (which turns out to come from Eberhard's cello!), forming the blood to the rhythm section's backbone as Rainer Br�ninghaus' keys and Volker's guitar (and, later, Eberhard's bass & cello) flit and fly around the sonosphere on this amazingly-well engineered song. So cool! (14.25/15)A2. "Prinz Eisenherz" (4:37) this one opens up with some ECM-like pristine sound rendering of double bass, acoustic guitar, multiple keyboards, and subtle percussion noises putting together a gentle yet full and subtly-nuanced motif. This interestingly-nuanced Mahavishnu-like whole group play continues throughout the song, start to finish, without the tempo ever clicking into gear (and never admitting Joe Nay's drums), just kind of floating on the top of the stream the whole way. Interesting! Amazing sonic clarity! It feels as if I can pick up every sound of each musician's hand movements. (8.875/10) A3. "Schnellh�rspiel" (5:26) Billy Cobham-like drums and Jan Hammer-like keyboard work open this high speed song as Eberhard and Volker add barks, yelps, and yowls from their own instruments as the music congeals into a Herbie Headhunter/Mahavishnu 2.0 train ride through the forests of Southern Germany. The technically-demanding high-speed multiple-instrument phrases are so like those pioneered by Chick Corea's Return To Forever's Hymn of the Seventh Galaxy and The Mahavishnu Orchestra's Birds of Fire (both 1973 releases) that it's amazing to hear them so soon coming from an European band. (Material like this and other elements of this album also remind me greatly of Todd Rundgren's own response to the Power Fusion phenomenon: his October release of the Todd Rundgren's Utopia album). Very impressive musicianship and sound production. (9.25/10)A4. "Mild Maniac" (5:08) a little smoother, a little more laid back, just as erudite and virtuosic despite the use of acoustic guitars, bowed cello and bass, gentle electric piano, and easier-on-the-brain melodies. These musicians are just so darn impressive! (9/10) B1. "The Visit" (7:26) loose though timed spaces in which all five musicians are freed to explore and express melodic lines and rhythms are punctuated by intermittent chord-and-drum punches as Volker and Rainer eventually "strike up a bargain" of flow and chord-commitment to which Joe, Peter, and Eberhard ascribe, resulting in the evolution in the third minute to a quirky little hook motif that sounds like a funky theme song to a television show (as was a fairly common phenomenon in 1974). By the arrival of the fourth minute that which sounded so quaint and almost trite (and yet expresses a Herbie Hancock-like level of sophistication and demand placed upon the musicians on hand) has evolved even further into something more akin to super funky Jan Hammer/George Duke song. Eberhard Weber and Joe Nay are simply phenomenal, as is Volker: shredding mercilessly away with his saw-like electric guitar tone until 6:50 when everything stops, leaving a steel-stringed acoustic guitar to finish things off before someone can be heard stomping across the floorboards on his exit from the recording room. Great stuff! (13.5/15)B2. "D-D�del" (12:12) dirty electric piano playing solo for the first two minutes of this before the rest of the band joins in with a BOB JAMES-like jazz-lite rendition of THE MARSHALL TUCKER BAND's 1973 hit song, "Can't You See" until the end of the fifth minute when everything devolves into a spacey, "Also Sprach Zarathustra" intro-like jazz atmosphere for Eberhard to have one of his "underwater" solos (this could be the first one I've heard of the sort that would become his trademark style and sound in a year or two). Eberhard eventually gathers steam: working his way into what becomes a very impressive display of full-fledged bass virtuosity--which the rest of the band responds to by joining in, each in turn exhibiting their own wildly-imaginative improvisations into the free jazz mix until the clock spring seems to reach its end, everything slowing down like the end of an Ever-Redi battery's charge to some children's toy. The end! Cool and eminently impressive! What a ride! Like a rollercoaster moving inside a slightly-disturbing amusement park funhouse. (22.625/25)Total time: 41:34A-/five stars; a minor masterpiece of eclectic but time-sensitive Third Wave Jazz-Rock Fusion that at times rivals some of the era's elite Power Fusion band outputs.
items._cn_summary: 这张1974年的专辑是德国吉他手Volker Kriegel领衔的爵士融合作品，以'Mild Maniac'为题，收录多首原创器乐曲。编曲上融合了放克贝斯线、电子键盘音色与吉他即兴对话，部分段落接近Mahavishnu Orchestra的复杂展开与Headhunters式的放克律动。开篇曲以双贝斯交织构建节奏骨架，键盘与吉他在音色空间内自由穿插；第二首以原声贝斯与多重键盘营造出类似ECM的透明声场；后续曲目以高速鼓击与键盘线条展开，融入器乐之间的呼应与对抗。整体制作注重录音清晰度与各乐器的层次分离，乐手之间的互动构成主要趣味。

items.body: La Feria returns to Liverpool this October for its eighth edition, spreading five days of Latin American music, theatre, dance, visual art and food from Hope Street down to Chinatown. The festival was launched in 2018 by Luma Creations, the Liverpool organisation led by Chilean-born songwriter Francisco Carrasco, to put artists from across Latin America and its British diaspora on the city’s stages. This year’s music starts in Chile, with songs built on the Andean rhythms of huayno and tinku and with folk tunes opened up through jazz improvisation. From there it moves to the brass-heavy mambo and salsa dura of a 13-piece Latin big band, to Afro-Colombian gaita flute set over electronic beats and deep bass, and to Brazilian forró and coco rhythms reworked as pop. Around the evening concerts and theatre performances, the week also brings a visual art exhibition, free workshops led by visiting artists, and two free family days to close the festival at the weekend. On Wednesday, Unity Theatre opens the festival with Manuelita, a one-woman show from Popelei in which Tamsin Hurtado Clarke takes on Manuela Sáenz. The Quito-born revolutionary fought through the independence wars at Simón Bolívar’s side, and in 1828 she helped him escape an attempt on his life in Bogotá. Hurtado Clarke tells her story through comedy and physical theatre to music by Colombian guitarist Camilo Menjura. Before the play, 18-year-old Argentine-British musician Eli Rowley plays Argentine and Andean tunes on the ronroco, a big-bodied, low-tuned relative of the charango, taking his cues from Gustavo Santaolalla and Jaime Torres. A short walk from Unity Theatre, the Music Room at Liverpool Philharmonic Hall takes over on Thursday, when Camila y Silvio return after selling out at La Feria in 2022. Camila Soria and Silvio Rozzi met during Chile’s student protests in 2011, and in 2015 they toured Argentina at length, learning the traditional styles of that country and the Andes. Their music moves between huayno, tinku, chacarera and vidala, with two voices over Rozzi’s guitar and charango and the deep thump of Soria’s bombo legüero. Fellow Chileans Peregrinos open the night. Guitarist Raimundo Santander and New York-based drummer Rodrigo Recabarren cut their first record together in Brooklyn in 2013, and they have used Chilean folk material as a starting point for improvisation ever since. By Friday the Music Room’s stage has to make space for thirteen musicians. Orchestra Mambo International came together in 2022 around Leeds salsa DJ Lubi Jovanovic and trombonist Jonny Enright to play the mambo of Tito Puente, Machito and Eddie Palmieri with a full big-band sound. Trumpets, trombone and baritone sax are stacked over piano, bass, vibraphone and a percussion section of bongos, congas and timbales. Since then they have written their own material, from mambos to cha-cha-chás, much of it gathered on their debut album Apúntalo. Up front, Venezuelan singer Carlos Peña, once a featured vocalist in Oscar D’León‘s orchestra, shares the vocals with Cuban singer Claritzel Miyares. It is the band’s first Liverpool show, and Cuban singer-songwriter George Peguero, returning to La Feria, opens the evening. Saturday night belongs to District, the club on Jordan Street in the Baltic Triangle, where Medellín producer Killabeatmaker sets Afro-Colombian and traditional Colombian rhythms over electronic beats and deep bass. His music keeps returning to the wildlife and landscapes of Colombia and the threats they face. On stage he beatboxes, raps and sings over live beats while Guadalupe Giraldo plays percussion and the gaita, the long, breathy duct flute of Colombia’s Caribbean coast. Opening the night, Mari Merenda plays her first ever UK show. The São Paulo singer/songwriter and producer built her name on videos of the asalato, a West African pair of seed-pod shakers knocked together on a cord. Her songs set forró and coco grooves against pop and R&B with electronic touches, most of them from her 2025 EP Reverbero. In Liverpool she switches between piano and asalato, with Guilherme Monteiro on bass, guitar and vocals, before moving on to Brighton and London. Before District opens its doors on Saturday night, World Museum on William Brown Street hands its galleries over to the festival for a free family day of music, dance, storytelling and workshops. The take-over is part of Cuerpos del Tiempo, a project with the museum’s Global Cultures Collections team to reimagine its Americas Gallery. Artists from eleven countries, from Argentina to Venezuela, perform among the displays. At midday Tamachij Chihuatl, a collective of more than 100 Indigenous Nahua women from Hueyapan in Puebla, Mexico, lead a food workshop. For forty years they have kept their village’s textile tradition alive, weaving wool and colouring it with natural dyes, and their name means “handmade”. La Feria’s free finale takes over The Black-E, the community arts centre on Great George Street, on Sunday. There, Orkney fiddler Catriona Price plays with El Guapo, a Buenos Aires duo on guitar, drums, percussion and vocals who mix Latin American roots with rock and funk. Together they run Routes to Roots, a project that brings musicians from different cultures together to write new music and rework traditional tunes, and which took them to the Edinburgh International Festival in August. Three dance companies share the day. London’s ArtPer UK bring Peruvian folk dances from the coast, the Andes and the Amazon, including the marinera norteña, a courtship dance in which couples circle each other waving handkerchiefs. Colibrí, a Manchester troupe of Mexican dancers led by Guerrero-born choreographer Magaly Flores, perform regional dances in traditional costume, from Veracruz and the Huasteca down to Oaxaca and Chiapas. Inti Tusuy, whose name is Quechua for “sun dance”, bring together dancers with roots in Bolivia, Mexico, Peru and the UK. Latin American food, DJs and dance workshops fill out the afternoon. Once the music stops at The Black-E on Sunday afternoon, the festival’s 2026 theme stays on the walls at Unity Theatre. Belonging, an exhibition by UK-based artists of Latin American heritage, runs there until 6th November, with work drawn from diaspora, ancestry and the places its makers call home.   Full programme and tickets are on the La Feria website The post Event Preview: La Feria 2026 (Liverpool; Wednesday 7th to Sunday 11th October 2026) appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body: Canadian electronic duo Delerium release their 16th studio album, “Exaudire”, on 22 January 2027 via Metropolis Records. The album arrives on regular CD and as a limited edition double vinyl pressed on oxblood-colored vinyl in a deluxe gatefold sleeve. The title “Exaudire” is Latin for listening, hearing and being heard. Metropolis Records describes the album as moving between the tangible and the dreamlike, built from electronic textures, expansive atmospheres and guest vocal performances. Side-Line previously reported on the album’s lead single, Into the Light, which embeds portions of Diamanda Galás’s 1986 recording “Deliver Me from Mine Enemies: IV. Ε Ξελόυ Mε (Deliver Me)” from her album “The Divine Punishment”. Exaudire by Delerium ‘Exaudire’ tracklist and guest vocalists The 12-track “Exaudire” features five different guest vocalists across its running order, confirmed via the album’s Bandcamp listing: “Higher Power” (feat. Mimi Page), “Into the Light” (feat. Diamanda Galás), “Dream Palace” (feat. Magic Wands), “Buried Light” (feat. Mimi Page), “Apocalypse” (feat. Inna Walters), “Stolen” (feat. Phildel), “Into the Unknown” (feat. Jaël), “Multiplying Zero” (feat. Inna Walters), “Chasing the Wind” (feat. Mimi Page), “Exaudire”, “Had to Go” (feat. Jaël) and “Litany” (feat. Mimi Page). Mimi Page is an American singer-songwriter and composer who has released four full-length albums since 2011. Magic Wands, a dream pop trio from Los Angeles, are also signed to Metropolis Records, with the albums “Switch” (2023) and “Cascades” (2025). Jaël, a Swiss singer, previously collaborated with Delerium on the 2003 EP “After All” and the album “Chimera”. Inna Walters, based in Nashville, already appeared on Delerium’s 2023 album “Signs”. Phildel is a classically trained English singer, pianist and songwriter from London. Delerium songs have previously appeared in the films “Brokedown Palace” and “Lara Croft: Tomb Raider”. “Silence”, the duo’s 2000 collaboration with Sarah McLachlan, was more recently heard in the BBC drama “Industry”. Side-Line also covered Peter Murphy and Boy George’s 2026 Delerium remix of “Let the Flowers Grow” and Restless Mosaic’s tribute track referencing the project. About Delerium Delerium was founded in Vancouver, Canada, in 1987 by Bill Leeb and original collaborator Michael Balch. Rhys Fulber later joined as Leeb’s main songwriting partner. Both Leeb and Fulber built their reputation in the electro-industrial group Front Line Assembly, and Delerium initially served as an outlet for dark, cinematic ambient soundscapes distinct from that project’s harder industrial sound. Early albums “Faces, Forms & Illusions” and “Morpheus” appeared in 1989. Through the 1990s, Delerium’s sound evolved from industrial electronics and ambient trance toward song-based electronic pop built around guest vocalists, a shift marked by 1994’s “Semantic Spaces”, which introduced a rotating cast of female singers on largely downtempo songs, a format the duo has used on every album since. “Karma” (1997) established Delerium’s more danceable side, and “Poem” (2000), produced with Chris Peterson, included “Silence” featuring Sarah McLachlan, which reached worldwide chart success and won a Juno Award in 2000. After the Leeb-Fulber reunion album “Chimera” (2003), Delerium continued through “Nuages du Monde” (2006), “Music Box Opera” (2012), the atmospheric “Mythologie” (2016) and “Signs” (2023), the latter featuring Inna Walters among other vocalists. “Exaudire” is Delerium’s 16th studio album and its first collaboration with Diamanda Galás.

items._cn_summary: 加拿大电子组合Delerium即将发行第十六张录音室专辑《Exaudire》，拉丁语意为聆听、倾听与被听见。专辑由Metropolis Records发行，包含标准CD与限量版双张黑血色乙烯基唱片。音乐被描述为在可触与梦境之间游走，以电子质感构建广阔氛围，并邀请五位客座女声参与十二首曲目。首发单曲《Into the Light》采样了Diamanda Galás 1986年作品中的段落，将极端人声与电子织体并置。客座阵容包括美国创作歌手Mimi Page、洛杉矶梦幻流行三人组Magic Wands、瑞士歌手Jaël、田纳西的Inna Walters以及伦敦古典训练出身的Phildel。乐评以新闻公告形式列出了曲目列表与合作者背景，并未对音乐本体进行深入分析或评论。

items.body: Belgian electronic dance act Lords Of Acid release their new album “Mundo Bizarro” digitally on 15 October 2026 via Metropolis Records. LP and CD formats follow on 9 November. The album is the group’s first collection of new material since 2018’s “Pretty in Kink”. “Mundo Bizarro” gathers the four singles Lords Of Acid have issued since April 2026, Karaoke Superstar (featuring Princess Superstar), Dream Boy (featuring Carla Harvey), “El Mundo Está Loco” (featuring Tony & The Kiki) and Ich Will Nur Dass (featuring Mari Kattman), alongside seven further new songs. The full tracklist, confirmed via the band’s Bandcamp page, runs: “Dreamboy”, “Dancing on the Flames”, “El Mundo Está Loco”, “Dopamine War”, “Maximo Roboto”, “Ich Will Nur Dass”, “City of Angels”, “So Stoned Today”, “Karaoke Superstar”, “You’re Obscene” and “A Viking’s Heart”. Mundo Bizarro by Lords Of Acid Carla Harvey, formerly co-lead vocalist of the American heavy rock band Butcher Babies, joined Lords Of Acid in January 2025, succeeding the late Ruth McArdle. The digital release of “Mundo Bizarro” coincides with the second leg of Lords Of Acid’s Cheeky Freaky North American tour, first announced in February 2026. At that time, the album carried the working title “Acid Reign”. The September 2026 press release from Metropolis Records confirms the final title as “Mundo Bizarro”. Specific October and November tour dates were not included in the current press materials. About Lords Of Acid Lords Of Acid formed in Antwerp, Belgium, in 1988, founded by Praga Khan together with Oliver Adams and Jade 4U. The group emerged from the hard-edged electronic dance scene of that era, blending techno, acid house and industrial music with lyrics centered on sexuality, drug use and hedonism. The band debuted with the New Beat single “I Sit on Acid”. Its first album, “Lust”, followed in 1991. “Voodoo-U”, with Ruth McArdle on vocals, arrived in 1994 and brought a heavier industrial dance sound along with the band’s best-known US club hits. “Our Little Secret” appeared in 1997. The B-side compilation “Heaven Is an Orgasm” (1998) and the remix album “Expand Your Head” (1999) came next. The rock-influenced “Farstucker”, featuring Deborah Ostrega, arrived in 2000. After a long gap, “Deep Chills” (2012) introduced Mea Fisher on vocals, and the Kickstarter-funded “Pretty in Kink” (2018) introduced Marieke Bresseleers. Metropolis Records remastered and reissued the band’s catalog from 2017 onward. Ruth McArdle died in 2024. Carla Harvey, previously of Butcher Babies, was announced as the band’s new lead vocalist in January 2025 and has since toured extensively with the group, including the 2025 “Praise The Lords” tour and the 2026 “Cheeky Freaky” tour. “Mundo Bizarro” is Harvey’s first full studio album with Lords Of Acid.
items._cn_summary: 比利时电子舞曲组合 Lords Of Acid 即将发行新专辑《Mundo Bizarro》，距离上一张专辑《Pretty in Kink》已有八年。这是已故主唱 Ruth McArdle 离世后、由前 Butcher Babies 成员 Carla Harvey 接任的首张作品，收录四首先行单曲与七首新歌。乐队自 1988 年成立以来始终以酸性浩室、工业电子和舞曲律动为底色，歌词围绕情欲、药物与享乐主义展开。该专辑延续了这一传统制作路线，与多位客座歌手合作，但并未展示出明显的风格转向或实验突破。整体定位偏向俱乐部场景的工业舞曲，独立厂牌 Metropolis Records 发行，保留了地下电子的基因但创新性有限。

items._cn_summary: Andrew Chalk的《The Golden Road》是一张极为稀有的环境音乐作品，于2007年录制、2025年以CD-R形式发行，仅限量25份并附有手工签名封套。整张专辑仅由一首长达33分钟的曲目构成，呈现出典型的氛围/嗡鸣（drone）音乐结构，无明显旋律推进，依赖音色的缓慢演变与声学空间的延展来构建聆听体验。Andrew Chalk长期活跃于英国地下实验音乐场景，作品多以极简手法探索声音质感本身。Faraway Press作为私人压制的微型厂牌，本身即体现了实体音乐文化中收藏与手工书志学的传统。然而，原文仅为唱片信息罗列，缺乏任何实际乐评内容或听感描述，信息严重不足，无法深入评估其艺术价值。

items._cn_summary: 这支曾以蓝眼灵魂乐见长的双人组合，在第五张专辑中转向爱尔兰民谣与蓝草风格。乐队借助主唱已故父亲的人脉网络，邀请到斯图尔特·邓肯与蒂姆·奥布莱恩等蓝草领域的知名乐手参与录制，整体制作相当扎实且具有相当的严肃度。不过乐评指出，在这一新方向的尝试中，成员偶尔难以抑制原有的创作惯性，蓝眼灵魂乐的痕迹不时浮现，使得作品同时与新派原声派系（neo-acoustic）的跨界气质产生呼应。整体而言，这是一次有诚意但仍处于探索阶段的风格转型，融合了传统美式民谣根基与跨界元素。

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items._cn_summary: 这是一张芬兰手风琴与钢琴二重奏专辑，由合作超过三十五年的搭档共同呈现。整体气质安静、流畅而梦幻，演奏以旋律为核心而非炫技，两位乐手在长期合作中形成的默契使得即兴段落能够超越乐谱自然展开。专辑包含传统曲目与原创作品，Kalaniemi的无词人声与Alakotila的钢琴相互呼应，弦乐四重奏在标题曲中以克制的编排扩展了音色层次。手风琴与钢琴的编制贯穿始终，偶尔引入探戈与皮亚佐拉元素，呈现北欧传统音乐在简约室内乐框架下的细腻表达。制作注重乐句的呼吸感与乐思的延展，适合作为背景聆听，传递出缓慢而温润的声响质地。

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.
Tiny Sun -
Vanishment
(Review)
Carolina Chocolate Drops -
Genuine Negro Jig
(Review)
items.label: Buda Musique
items._genre: musette / ragtime / jug band / French chanson / eclectic folk
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Dominique Cravic与Les Primitifs du futur的第五张录音，延续了与地下漫画家Robert Crumb的合作。乐评形容其声响如同在堆满78转唱片的阁楼中翻找灵感，以手风琴、萨克斯、班卓琴、曼陀林、口琴、锯琴、夏威夷吉他、风笛管等琳琅乐器演绎二十七首短曲，跨越巴尔-缪赛特、拉格泰姆、爵士乐、法国香颂、民间小调等多种二十世纪初期的风格。Cravic的演唱近似念白，带有Maurice Chevalier式的平民气质。专辑收录对已故法国抵抗运动歌手Juliette Gréco的致敬作品，并以幽默方式重新演绎1925年的《Ukulele Lady》等老歌。乐评将其与Dan Hicks & His Hot Licks相提并论，认为这些被遗忘的音乐与被放弃的风格在严肃而热情的演绎下重获新生。整体定位为带有学术趣味的复古杂锦式合辑，跨界融合度较高但实验性有限。

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets

items._genre: folk / historical ballad / Lancashire industrial ballad
items._cn_summary: 这是一张以1819年曼彻斯特彼得洛大屠杀为题材的概念专辑，由Young 'Uns成员Sean Cooney创作，以原创民谣形式重构这一英国工人运动史上的标志性事件。专辑以书配CD的形式呈现，收录当代信件、政治漫画与插图，构成多媒体项目。Cooney擅长从个人视角切入历史，聚焦Sam Bamford、Mary Fildes等小人物故事，同时以三部短曲描绘士兵的傲慢与残暴。Eliza Carthy的小提琴与人声、Sam Carter的吉他、Jennifer Reid的兰开夏工业民谣演唱与旁白共同构建出层次丰富的声景，捕捉集会期待、骑兵冲击的恐惧与悲痛的余波。在全球抗议空间收紧的当下，专辑成为对历史与当下权力关系的沉稳提醒。

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�
items.label: Mig
items._genre: New Orleans R&B / funk / blues / Mardi Gras revue
items._cn_summary: 这张现场专辑记录了Dr. John在德国莱茵河畔罗蕾莱露天剧场的演出，以新奥尔良传统为根基，融合R&B、放克与布鲁斯元素，呈现出Mardi Gras式的狂欢现场感。演出以经典'Iko Iko'开场，涵盖'I Walk on Guilded Splinters'等迷幻funk作品以及自创的'Sweet Home New Orleans''Goin' Back to New Orleans'等曲目，末尾以Earl King的'Big Chief'收束。伴奏乐队为低音、吉他与鼓的紧凑四人编制，演奏风格沉稳而富有节奏推动力。整张专辑在声乐、钢琴和滑音吉他之间游走，展现了浓郁的巫毒文化意象与新奥尔良地方色彩。文中引用了Dr. John本人的话作为创作理念：'演奏一切可能的东西，旧、中、新乃至尚未存在之物。'专辑同时附有CD与DVD媒介，完整呈现了现场氛围与观众互动。

Williams和Alex Townend在暌违十年后携新专辑回归。文章以轻松幽默的对话开篇，展现了两人对心理健康话题的坦然态度，以及他们从过去刻意模糊、制造混乱的采访风格转变为更加真诚开放的交流方式。他们自称是ATP（All Tomorrow's Parties）系列的'回头的浪子'，暗示其与英国独立音乐场景的紧密关联。然而，文章截取的内容较短，主要聚焦于采访本身的氛围和人物状态，未深入涉及新专辑的音乐结构、编曲手法或制作细节，也未提供具体的音响美学分析。整体更像是新闻性的人物特写而非深度乐评，对音乐内容的实质性探讨有限。
